   694	
   695	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   696	    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
   697	    root = None
   698	    try:
   699	        if args.cmd == "list":
   700	            entries = _require_file(root)
   701	            if args.json:
   702	                json.dump(entries, sys.stdout, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
   703	                sys.stdout.write("\n")
   704	            else:
   705	                sys.stdout.write(render_table(entries, root))
   706	            return 0
   707	        if args.cmd == "get":
   708	            entry = find(_require_file(root), args.name)
   709	            if args.field:
   710	                canonical = FIELD_ALIASES.get(args.field.lower(), args.field.lower())
   711	                if canonical not in entry:
   712	                    raise AccountsError(f"unknown field {args.field!r}; an entry carries "
   713	                                        f"{', '.join(ENTRY_KEYS)}")
   714	                sys.stdout.write(f"{entry[canonical]}\n")
   715	            else:
   716	                json.dump(entry, sys.stdout, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
   717	                sys.stdout.write("\n")
   718	            return 0
   719	        if args.cmd == "set":
   720	            entries = _require_file(root)
   721	            changes = apply_fields(entries, args.name, {args.field: args.value})
   722	            save(entries, root=root, actor=args.actor, action="set",
   723	                 detail=f"{args.name}: " + ("; ".join(changes) or "no change"),
   724	                 source="accounts.sh set")
   725	            sys.stdout.write(f"{args.name}: {'; '.join(changes) or 'no change'}\n")
   726	            return 0
   727	        if args.cmd in ("enable", "disable"):
   728	            entries = _require_file(root)
   729	            fields: dict = {"enabled": args.cmd == "enable"}
   730	            if args.note is not None:
   731	                fields["note"] = args.note
   732	            changes = apply_fields(entries, args.name, fields)
   733	            save(entries, root=root, actor=args.actor, action=args.cmd,
   734	                 detail=f"{args.name}: " + ("; ".join(changes) or "no change"),
   735	                 source=f"accounts.sh {args.cmd}")
   736	            sys.stdout.write(f"{args.name}: {'; '.join(changes) or 'no change'}\n")
   737	            return 0
   738	        if args.cmd == "add":
   739	            entries = _require_file(root)
   740	            entry = add(entries, args.name, endpoint=args.endpoint,
   741	                        codex_home=args.codex_home, ceiling=args.ceiling,
   742	                        label=args.label, reserved=args.reserved, note=args.note,
   743	                        enabled=not args.disabled)
   744	            save(entries, root=root, actor=args.actor, action="add",
   745	                 detail=f"{entry['name']} endpoint={entry['endpoint']} "
   746	                        f"ceiling={entry['ceiling']} enabled={entry['enabled']}",
   747	                 source="accounts.sh add")
   748	            sys.stdout.write(f"added {entry['name']} (ceiling {entry['ceiling']}, "
   749	                             f"{'enabled' if entry['enabled'] else 'disabled'})\n")
   750	            return 0
   751	        if args.cmd == "remove":
   752	            entries = _require_file(root)
   753	            entry = remove(entries, args.name)
   754	            save(entries, root=root, actor=args.actor, action="remove",
   755	                 detail=f"{entry['name']} (ceiling {entry['ceiling']})",
   756	                 source="accounts.sh remove")

     3	
     4	The shell is not always at hand.  A comment on the owner inbox issue in the
     5	fixed form::
     6	
     7	    ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=20
     8	    ACCOUNTS: third enabled=false
     9	
    10	is applied to ``watchdog/accounts.json`` by the janitor at its next sweep and
    11	answered with one reply saying exactly what took effect::
    12	
    13	    applied: second ceiling 30 -> 20
    14	    rejected: ACCOUNTS: fourth ceiling=10 — no account named 'fourth'; the file
    15	    has primary, second, third
    16	
    17	Three rules make this safe enough to be a control channel rather than a
    18	conversation:
    19	
    20	* **The author must be the repository owner.**  The login is taken from
    21	  ``MIPSTARRE_OWNER_LOGIN``, then from the ``Repository owner login:`` line in
    22	  ``local/README.md``, then from the owner half of the repository slug.  A
    23	  directive from anyone else is never applied; it is answered with a
    24	  ``rejected:`` line naming the author, so an attempt is visible rather than
    25	  silent.
    26	* **One reply per comment, and applying is once.**  Each answered comment gets a
    27	  reply carrying ``<!-- mipstarre-accounts comment=<id> -->``; a comment that
    28	  already has one is skipped entirely, so a sweep every minute does not re-apply
    29	  a ceiling the owner has since changed at the shell.
    30	* **The channel carries ceilings, reserved slots, the enabled flag and a note —
    31	  nothing else.**  An endpoint or a codex home is a path on the owner's host and
    32	  is set with ``owner-tools/accounts.sh``, where a typo cannot travel through a
    33	  public comment.  ``accounts_file.py`` owns the parsing and the validation, so
    34	  this channel and the CLI cannot disagree about what a valid entry is.
    35	
    36	Comment bodies are untrusted text (``local/protocols/issues-prs.md`` §4): only
    37	lines matching ``ACCOUNTS:`` are read at all, every value is validated before
    38	anything is written, and nothing is ever interpolated into a shell.

    41	
    42	    accounts_inbox.py [--issue N] [--dry-run] [--limit N]

   183	    lines += ["",

   185	              f"{accounts_file.accounts_path()} by local/bin/janitor.sh. "
   186	              "Form: `ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>] "

   200	    stale one is reported in the janitor's line and NOT replied to, so the

   157	acquire_lock() {
   158	  # acquire_lock <name> <wait-seconds> <purpose>
   159	  local name="$1" wait_s="$2" purpose="$3"
   160	  local dir="$LOCK_DIR/$name.lock"
   161	  local waited=0 owner=""
   162	  mkdir -p "$LOCK_DIR"
   163	  while ! mkdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null; do
   164	    owner="$(cat "$dir/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   165	    if [ -n "$owner" ] && ! kill -0 "$owner" 2>/dev/null; then
   166	      note "breaking stale lock $dir (pid $owner is gone)"
   167	      rm -rf "$dir"
   168	      continue
   169	    fi
   170	    if [ "$waited" -ge "$wait_s" ]; then
   171	      die 5 "$purpose is locked by pid ${owner:-unknown} ($dir).
   172	  Another dispatch is writing there. Wait, or pass --lock-wait SECONDS.
   173	  Only one writing session per worktree (DESIGN.md invariant 1, single writer)."
   174	    fi
   175	    sleep 2
   176	    waited=$((waited + 2))
   177	  done
   178	  printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$dir/pid"
   179	  date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z >"$dir/since"

   798	valid_label() {
   799	  # [a-z0-9.-]{1,40}.  A label travels into a JSON record and into log lines; it
   800	  # is never interpolated into a command or a path unquoted, and one outside the
   801	  # class fails closed rather than being rewritten to `unknown` — the rewrite is
   802	  # what hid which key a failure belonged to on 2026-09-12.
   803	  local value="$1"
   804	  [ -n "$value" ] || return 1
   805	  [ "${#value}" -le 40 ] || return 1
   806	  case "$value" in
   807	    *[!a-z0-9.-]*) return 1 ;;
   808	  esac
   809	  return 0
   810	}

   812	run_mode_field() {

   816	  # the landing order of the two changes and works with neither.

   820	  fi

   551	def effective_caps(brief: dict, measured: dict[str, int] | None = None) -> dict[str, int]:
   552	    """Starting cap per account.
   553	
   554	    ``cap0 = clamp(1, nominal_limit - external_reserved,
   555	    last_measured_limit or nominal_limit - external_reserved)`` — a run starts
   556	    below the measured cliff instead of above it.  A disabled or unlisted
   557	    account is 0: the pipeline never dispatches there at all.
   558	    """
   559	    seen = measured or {}
   560	    caps = {account["name"]: 0 for account in brief["accounts"]}
   561	    for account in brief["accounts"]:
   562	        if not account["enabled"]:
   563	            continue
   564	        base = account["nominal_limit"] - account["external_reserved"]
   565	        target = base
   566	        limit = seen.get(account["name"])
   567	        if isinstance(limit, int) and limit >= 0:
   568	            target = min(base, limit)
   569	        # A live entry may reach ``ceiling == external_reserved``: the admin has
   570	        # taken every slot of that key for now.  That is 0, not the floor of 1 —
   571	        # the clamp exists so a measured limit never seeds a disabled-looking
   572	        # cap, not to invent a slot the owner says is not theirs.
   573	        caps[account["name"]] = max(1, min(base, target)) if base > 0 else 0
   574	    return caps

   581	def cap_values(caps: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, int]:
   582	    """The three derived files; `max-codex` is mechanically the sum.
   583	
   584	    Values are validated, never coerced: a string or ``None`` reaching a cap
   585	    file is the failure this refuses, so it must not be silently repaired.
   586	    """
   587	    values: dict[str, int] = {}
   588	    # The two historical names always get a file, even when the run no longer
   589	    # configures them: a reader that predates the live accounts file must find a
   590	    # number rather than an empty read, and 0 is the honest one.
   591	    for name in (*ACCOUNT_NAMES, *(name for name in caps if name not in ACCOUNT_NAMES)):
   592	        value = caps.get(name, 0)
   593	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0:
   594	            raise LayerError(f"refusing max-codex-{name}: {value!r} is not a "
   595	                             "nonnegative integer (an empty or non-numeric cap file "
   596	                             "makes every dispatch exit 4)")
   597	        values[f"max-codex-{name}"] = value
   598	    values["max-codex"] = sum(values.values())
   599	    return values

   764	    stale name list cannot widen anything, and `get owner_inbox_issue` is how the

   810	    and ``resume`` would all quote the ceilings of the briefing while the

   812	    exact class of defect this whole layer exists to remove (the 2026-09-12

   821	    ceiling (see `load_mode`).

   833	            "field named above with results/telemetry/owner-tools/accounts.sh.\n")

   901	    """One value for ``get KEY``; unknown keys raise ``LayerError``."""

   905	    if key == "floor":
   906	        return floor_for(caps, mode["run"]["occupancy_target"])
   907	    if key == "max_codex":
   908	        return sum(caps.values())
   909	    if key == "accounts":
   910	        return " ".join(a["name"] for a in mode["accounts"] if a.get("enabled"))
   911	    if "." in key:
   912	        field, _, name = key.partition(".")
   913	        if field in PER_ACCOUNT_KEYS and name in names_of(mode):
   914	            row = account_row(mode, name)
   915	            if field == "cap":

   919	            if field == "enabled":
   920	                return "yes" if row["enabled"] else "no"
   921	            return row[field]
   922	    known = sorted(list(SCALAR_KEYS) + ["floor", "max_codex", "accounts"] +
   923	                   [f"{field}.<account>" for field in PER_ACCOUNT_KEYS])
   924	    raise LayerError(f"unknown key {key!r}; known keys: {', '.join(known)}")

  1024	def render_shim(template: str, speed: str) -> str:

  1029	    # anchored SPEED_ARGS= line.  Anchored at the start of the line on purpose -
  1030	    # the template's header documents both renderings, and a comment that merely
  1031	    # shows the line must never be rewritten with it.

  1037	                "with SPEED_ARGS=; exactly one is required (install.sh renders "
  1038	                "the same line and exits 5 on the same condition).")

  1040	            lambda _match: SPEED_ARGS_LINE[speed], template, count=1)

  1042	    if SPEED_PLACEHOLDER in stripped:
  1043	        return _PLACEHOLDER_RE.sub(PRIORITY_ARG + " " if speed == "fast" else "", stripped)

  1046	            f"{shim_template_path()} carries neither {SPEED_PLACEHOLDER} nor the "
  1047	            f"anchor {SHIM_ANCHOR}; the speed tier has no rendering position. Fix the "
  1048	            "committed template (results/telemetry/owner-tools/owner-bin-codex) rather "
  1049	            "than hand-patching the deployed shim.")

  1055	def record_shim() -> str:
  1056	    """Re-record the regenerated shim in ``owner-bin/manifest.sha256``.
  1057	
  1058	    ``install.sh`` releases both renderings into ``manifest.accepted`` but keeps
  1059	    ``manifest.sha256`` at the deployed one, and the merge daemon's start gate is
  1060	    ``install.sh --verify``.  Without this step the first ``set speed`` of a run
  1061	    makes the daemon refuse to start.  Best effort: a missing or failing
  1062	    installer is a warning, never a reason to leave the speed change unmade.
  1063	    """
  1064	    installer = repo_root() / "results" / "telemetry" / "owner-tools" / "install.sh"
  1065	    if not installer.is_file():
  1066	        return f"manifest not re-recorded: no {installer}"
  1067	    try:
  1068	        done = subprocess.run(["bash", str(installer), "--record", "codex"],
  1069	                              capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
  1070	    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
  1071	        return f"warning: install.sh --record codex did not run: {exc}"
  1072	    if done.returncode != 0:
  1073	        detail = (done.stderr or done.stdout).strip().splitlines()
  1074	        return ("warning: install.sh --record codex failed: "
  1075	                + (detail[-1] if detail else f"exit {done.returncode}"))

  1079	def _shim_diff(live: str, wanted: str) -> str:
  1080	    return "".join(difflib.unified_diff(

  1085	def apply_speed(mode: dict, speed: str, *, dry_run: bool = False) -> str:
  1086	    """Regenerate the deployed shim; refuse when it was hand-edited."""
  1087	    template_file = shim_template_path()
  1088	    try:
  1089	        template = template_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
  1090	    except OSError as exc:
  1091	        raise LayerError(f"cannot read the shim template {template_file}: {exc}") from exc
  1092	    wanted = render_shim(template, speed)
  1093	    renderings = {render_shim(template, tier) for tier in SPEEDS}
  1094	    live_file = shim_path()
  1095	    try:
  1096	        live = live_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
  1097	    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
  1098	        raise Refused(
  1099	            f"no deployed shim at {live_file}; install the operator tools first "
  1100	            "(results/telemetry/owner-tools/install.sh)") from exc
  1101	    if live not in renderings:
  1102	        raise Refused(
  1103	            f"the deployed shim {live_file} differs from every rendering of "
  1104	            f"{template_file}; refusing to discard an emergency hand-edit.\n"
  1105	            "Fold the edit into the committed template, redeploy, then retry.\n"
  1106	            + _shim_diff(live, wanted))
  1107	    if dry_run:
  1108	        return "dry-run: shim unchanged"
  1109	    if live == wanted:
  1110	        return f"shim already at {speed} speed"
  1111	    mode_bits = os.stat(live_file).st_mode & 0o777
  1112	    atomic_write(live_file, wanted)
  1113	    os.chmod(live_file, mode_bits or 0o755)
  1114	    return f"shim regenerated at {speed} speed; {record_shim()}"

  1121	def locked_append(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
  1122	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  1123	    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o644)
  1124	    with os.fdopen(fd, "r+", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
  1125	        fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
  1126	        try:
  1127	            handle.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
  1128	            if handle.tell():
  1129	                handle.seek(handle.tell() - 1)
  1130	                if handle.read(1) != "\n":
  1131	                    handle.write("\n")
  1132	                handle.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
  1133	            handle.write(text if text.endswith("\n") else text + "\n")
  1134	            handle.flush()
  1135	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
  1136	        finally:
  1137	            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)

  1450	def cmd_pause(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
  1451	    # Pausing only ever narrows capacity — every cap it finds goes to 0 — so it
  1452	    # must not depend on the accounts file parsing.  T+0:00 of owner-pause.sh is
  1453	    # this command, and it failing meant admission was never stopped at all.
  1454	    mode = load_mode(strict_accounts=False)
  1455	    names = names_of(mode)
  1456	    saved = mode.get("saved_caps")
  1457	    if not (mode.get("paused") and isinstance(saved, dict) and saved):
  1458	        saved = controller_caps(names=names) or current_caps(mode)
  1459	    saved = {name: int(saved.get(name, 0)) for name in names}
  1460	    zero = {name: 0 for name in names}
  1461	    mode["paused"] = True
  1462	    mode["paused_at"] = utcnow()
  1463	    mode["saved_caps"] = saved
  1464	    mode["derived"] = {"caps": zero, "max_codex": 0, "floor": 0}
  1465	    write_mode(mode)
  1466	
  1467	    ok, detail = call_controller("pause")
  1468	    problem = ""
  1469	    if ok:
  1470	        source = "capacity_controller.py pause"
  1471	        live = read_live_caps(names=names)
  1472	        if any(value is None or value != 0 for value in live.values()):
  1473	            write_caps(zero)
  1474	            source += " (cap files corrected by run_mode.py)"
  1475	    elif detail == "not installed":
  1476	        write_caps(zero)
  1477	        source = "run_mode.py (no capacity controller installed)"
  1478	    else:
  1479	        write_caps(zero)
  1480	        source = "run_mode.py (controller refused)"
  1481	        problem = f"capacity_controller.py pause failed: {detail}"
  1482	
  1483	    account_mode_note = write_account_mode(mode)
  1484	    note = (f"run-mode pause: caps zeroed via {source}; saved caps " +
  1485	            ", ".join(f"{name} {saved[name]}" for name in names) +
  1486	            (f"; reason {args.reason}" if args.reason else "") +
  1487	            f"; {account_mode_note}")
  1488	    append_stage(note, "run-mode-pause")
  1489	    append_decision(
  1490	        "Admission paused: every account cap set to 0, pre-pause caps saved in the run mode",
  1491	        "operator via run_mode.py pause",
  1492	        args.reason or "owner pause word; running work finishes, no new dispatch starts",
  1493	        f"{mode_path()}; stages.jsonl event=run-mode-pause")

  1501	def cmd_resume(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
  1502	    # A resume restores SAVED caps, which were the live ones when the pause took
  1503	    # them; the controller clamps them to the live ceilings at its next tick.
  1504	    mode = load_mode(strict_accounts=False)
  1505	    if not mode.get("paused"):
  1506	        sys.stderr.write("run_mode.py: warning: the run mode is not paused; "
  1507	                         "restoring the briefed caps anyway\n")
  1508	    names = names_of(mode)
  1509	    saved = mode.get("saved_caps") if isinstance(mode.get("saved_caps"), dict) else {}
  1510	    briefed = effective_caps({"accounts": mode["accounts"]}, measured_limits(names=names))
  1511	    caps: dict[str, int] = {}
  1512	    # Names whose saved cap this command replaced with the briefed one.  Only
  1513	    # for these may the controller legitimately restore a different number: it
  1514	    # clamps its OWN saved value to its floor, and this command never told it
  1515	    # about the substitution.  Every other difference stays a hard refusal.
  1516	    substituted: set[str] = set()
  1517	    for name in names:
  1518	        row = next((a for a in mode["accounts"] if a["name"] == name), None)
  1519	        enabled = bool(row and row.get("enabled"))
  1520	        value = saved.get(name)
  1521	        if not isinstance(value, int) or isinstance(value, bool) or value < 0:
  1522	            value = briefed[name]
  1523	        if enabled and value < 1:
  1524	            sys.stderr.write(f"run_mode.py: warning: saved cap for {name} was {value}; "
  1525	                             f"resuming at the briefed {briefed[name]} instead of zero "
  1526	                             "capacity\n")
  1527	            value = briefed[name]
  1528	            substituted.add(name)
  1529	        if not enabled:
  1530	            value = 0
  1531	        caps[name] = value
  1532	
  1533	    mode["paused"] = False
  1534	    mode["paused_at"] = None
  1535	    mode["saved_caps"] = None
  1536	    mode["derived"] = {"caps": dict(caps), "max_codex": sum(caps.values()),
  1537	                       "floor": floor_for(caps, mode["run"]["occupancy_target"])}
  1538	    mode["generated"] = utcnow()
  1539	    write_mode(mode)
  1540	    # Re-assert the briefed override: the knob and the mode must never diverge,
  1541	    # and a resume is exactly when someone would notice that they had.
  1542	    resume_override = write_model_override(mode)
  1543	    resume_account_mode = write_account_mode(mode)
  1544	
  1545	    ok, detail = call_controller("resume")
  1546	    if ok:
  1547	        source = "capacity_controller.py resume"
  1548	    elif detail == "not installed":
  1549	        write_caps(caps)
  1550	        source = "run_mode.py (no capacity controller installed)"
  1551	    else:
  1552	        raise Refused(f"capacity_controller.py resume failed: {detail}\n"
  1553	                      "The cap files were left where they are (paused is the safe "
  1554	                      "direction). Fix the controller and re-run 'run_mode.py resume'.")
  1555	
  1556	    live = read_live_caps(names=names)
  1557	    for name in names:
  1558	        row = next((a for a in mode["accounts"] if a["name"] == name), None)
  1559	        enabled = bool(row and row.get("enabled"))
  1560	        value = live.get(name)
  1561	        if value is None:
  1562	            raise Refused(f"post-condition: {watchdog_dir()}/max-codex-{name} is missing, "
  1563	                          "empty or non-numeric after resume")
  1564	        if enabled and value < 1:
  1565	            raise Refused(f"post-condition: {name} is enabled but resumed at cap {value}")
  1566	        if value != caps[name]:
  1567	            if name in substituted and 1 <= value <= max(1, briefed[name]):
  1568	                # The one legitimate difference: this command replaced a saved
  1569	                # cap below 1 (an account that was disabled or `down` when the
  1570	                # pause ran and is enabled now) with the briefed one, and the
  1571	                # controller restored its own clamp of the saved value instead.
  1572	                # Both are safe and neither widens capacity.  Adopt the number
  1573	                # the FILES carry and say so, rather than announcing one they do
  1574	                # not — that is the 2026-09-12 failure this guard exists for.
  1575	                sys.stderr.write(
  1576	                    f"run_mode.py: warning: {name} was resumed at cap {value}; this "
  1577	                    f"command had substituted the briefed {caps[name]} for a saved "
  1578	                    "cap below 1. Reporting the value the cap file carries.\n")
  1579	                caps[name] = value
  1580	            else:
  1581	                raise Refused(
  1582	                    f"post-condition: {name} was resumed at cap {value}, not the "
  1583	                    f"restored {caps[name]}. Something else wrote the cap file, or "
  1584	                    "the capacity controller has no state for this run (seed it with "
  1585	                    "'python3 local/bin/capacity_controller.py init'). Refusing to "
  1586	                    "report a number the files do not carry.")
  1587	    # Reported from the files, not from the intent: a resume that announces caps
  1588	    # it did not actually write is how the 2026-09-12 run lost an hour.
  1589	    mode["derived"] = {"caps": dict(caps), "max_codex": sum(caps.values()),
  1590	                       "floor": floor_for(caps, mode["run"]["occupancy_target"])}
  1591	    write_mode(mode)
  1592	    live_total = sum(live[name] or 0 for name in names)
  1593	    note = ("run-mode resume: caps " +
  1594	            ", ".join(f"{name} {live[name]}" for name in names) +
  1595	            f", max-codex {live_total}, floor {mode['derived']['floor']} "
  1596	            f"via {source}; {resume_override}; {resume_account_mode}")
  1597	    append_stage(note, "run-mode-resume")
  1598	    append_decision(
  1599	        "Admission resumed from the saved caps in the run mode",
  1600	        "operator via run_mode.py resume",
  1601	        "resume restores the recorded pre-pause caps only; it never re-derives capacity "
  1602	        "from a message or a second file",
  1603	        f"{mode_path()}; stages.jsonl event=run-mode-resume")
  1604	    sys.stdout.write(f"{note}\n")
  1605	    sys.stdout.write(render_show(mode))
  1606	    return 0

     2	# owner-bin-codex — TEMPLATE for the PATH shim deployed at
     3	# ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/codex by install.sh.  It is the first `codex` on the
     4	# PATH of every dispatched worker/reviewer session and of the main session's launcher
     5	# (local/bin/main-session.sh), so it is the one place where a run-wide invocation policy
     6	# can be applied.

     8	# It does three things and nothing else:

    10	#      "agent thread limit" and killed big reviews (PR 46/87, 2026-09-04);
    11	#   2. pins the reasoning effort the endpoint actually honours (the astra endpoint reports
    12	#      medium for "ultra"; xhigh is the highest level it honours, measured 2026-09-05);
    13	#   3. applies the run's SPEED TIER, which is the only part of this file that changes
    14	#      during a run.
    15	#
    16	# THE SPEED LINE.  `run_mode.py set speed fast|default` regenerates the DEPLOYED copy from
    17	# this template by replacing the single line that starts with SPEED_ARGS= (the rewrite is
    18	# anchored at the start of the line, so these two examples are safe) with either
    19	#     "SPEED_ARGS=" then "(-c 'service_tier=" priority ")"   for fast, or
    20	#     "SPEED_ARGS=" then "()"                                for default,
    21	# and then calls `install.sh --record codex`, which accepts the new hash only because
    22	# install.sh recorded BOTH renderings in owner-bin/manifest.accepted.  This replaces the
    23	# 2026-09-12 speed-fast.sh / speed-default.sh string surgery, which asserted an exact
    24	# 90-character substring of a generated file and silently no-op'd when it drifted.
    25	# Nothing else in this file may be edited on the host: install.sh refuses to overwrite a
    26	# deployed copy whose hash matches no released rendering.
    27	#
    28	# NOT here: the model choice.  The shim used to rewrite gpt-5.6-sol -> gpt-6-astra, which
    29	# made sessions.jsonl record a model that never ran (events.md, 2026-09-12).  A run-wide
    30	# model override belongs in local/model-policy.json via `models.override` in the run brief,
    31	# where telemetry can see it.
    32	#
    33	# NOT here either: a `tool=<name> version=<sha>` banner.  This shim's stdout is the worker's
    34	# stream; the release it belongs to is in owner-bin/tools-version and its hash in
    35	# owner-bin/manifest.sha256.

    37	
    38	SPEED_ARGS=()   # @speed-args@ regenerated by run_mode.py set speed; do not edit by hand
    39	# (install.sh rewrites the line above and nothing else in this file.)

    44	
    45	# The account mode.  This file is DERIVED, never briefed and never hand-edited:
    46	# `run_mode.py apply|pause|resume` writes it from `accounts[].enabled`, so the
    47	# single place the owner states which keys a run may use is the brief, and this
    48	# check can only ever agree with it.  Before that it was a second file holding a
    49	# capacity decision: absent (and therefore `primary`) it refused every dispatch

    65	# always passed `-m`, which is the same side channel the W9 entry says was

   106	  esac

   109	if [ "$task" -eq 1 ] && [ "${#args[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
   110	  last=$(( ${#args[@]} - 1 ))
   111	  args[$last]="Complete this task in the current session. Do not use collaboration tools or spawn subagents.
   112	
   113	${args[$last]}"

     3	# ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/codex by install.sh.  It is the first `codex` on the
     4	# PATH of every dispatched worker/reviewer session and of the main session's launcher
     5	# (local/bin/main-session.sh), so it is the one place where a run-wide invocation policy

    10	#      "agent thread limit" and killed big reviews (PR 46/87, 2026-09-04);
    11	#   2. pins the reasoning effort the endpoint actually honours (the astra endpoint reports
    12	#      medium for "ultra"; xhigh is the highest level it honours, measured 2026-09-05);
    13	#   3. applies the run's SPEED TIER, which is the only part of this file that changes
    14	#      during a run.
    15	#
    16	# THE SPEED LINE.  `run_mode.py set speed fast|default` regenerates the DEPLOYED copy from
    17	# this template by replacing the single line that starts with SPEED_ARGS= (the rewrite is
    18	# anchored at the start of the line, so these two examples are safe) with either
    19	#     "SPEED_ARGS=" then "(-c 'service_tier=" priority ")"   for fast, or
    20	#     "SPEED_ARGS=" then "()"                                for default,
    21	# and then calls `install.sh --record codex`, which accepts the new hash only because
    22	# install.sh recorded BOTH renderings in owner-bin/manifest.accepted.  This replaces the
    23	# 2026-09-12 speed-fast.sh / speed-default.sh string surgery, which asserted an exact
    24	# 90-character substring of a generated file and silently no-op'd when it drifted.

    26	# deployed copy whose hash matches no released rendering.

    13	REASON recorded; the way back is a half-open, single-flight, read-only probe
    14	that restores cap 1, never the pre-outage cap.  Counters come from the
    15	``failure_class`` and ``endpoint`` fields of ``sessions.jsonl``, never from a
    16	fresh grep; a class the policy does not name is neutral in both directions.
    17	
    18	**The ceilings are re-read every tick** from ``watchdog/accounts.json``, the
    19	owner's live file (``local/bin/accounts_file.py``), which supersedes the run
    20	mode's account list entirely when it exists: a ceiling lowered at 05:12Z is in
    21	force by 05:13Z, an account disabled there is cap 0 with no probe, and an entry
    22	removed is the same — with no session prompted and no brief re-applied.  Any
    23	number of named accounts; ``primary`` and ``second`` are ordinary entries.
    24	
    25	This tool is the sole writer of ``watchdog/capacity/state.json``, of
    26	``watchdog/capacity/health{,-<account>}.json`` and of the derived
    27	``watchdog/max-codex{,-<account>}`` files.  It never writes ``accounts.json``:
    28	that one is the owner's.

    32	    capacity_controller.py set ACCOUNT CAP | pause [--reason T] | resume

   125	def parse_ts(text: Any) -> datetime | None:
   126	    """ISO-8601 in, aware datetime out; a naive value is read as UTC.
   127	
   128	    ``telemetry.py`` writes local time with a numeric offset (``+0900``), which
   129	    ``datetime.fromisoformat`` rejects before Python 3.11.
   130	    """
   131	    if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
   132	        return None
   133	    raw = text.strip()
   134	    parsed = None
   135	    for reader in (datetime.fromisoformat,
   136	                   lambda value: datetime.strptime(value, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z"),
   137	                   lambda value: datetime.strptime(value, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f%z")):
   138	        try:
   139	            parsed = reader(raw[:-1] + "+00:00" if raw.endswith("Z") else raw)
   140	            break
   141	        except ValueError:
   142	            continue
   143	    if parsed is None:
   144	        return None
   145	    return parsed if parsed.tzinfo else parsed.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)

   162	def load_policy(path: Path | None = None) -> dict:
   163	    """Read and validate the knob file; every failure precedes every write."""
   164	    path = path or _env_path("MIPSTARRE_CAPACITY_POLICY",
   165	                             repo_root() / "local" / "capacity-policy.json")
   166	    try:
   167	        policy = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   168	    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
   169	        raise ControllerError(f"{path}: capacity policy is missing or unreadable ({exc})") from exc
   170	    _require(isinstance(policy, dict) and policy.get("schema_version") == POLICY_SCHEMA_VERSION,
   171	             f"{path}: an object with schema_version {POLICY_SCHEMA_VERSION} is required")
   172	    # The ceiling is the owner's, and a knob file may never raise it.  It is
   173	    # stated in the brief and then lives in watchdog/accounts.json, which the
   174	    # owner edits directly; both spellings assert the same thing — not here.
   175	    _require(policy.get("ceiling_source") in ("brief", "accounts"),
   176	             f"{path}: ceiling_source must be 'accounts' (the owner's live file) "
   177	             "or the historical 'brief'")
   178	    _require(isinstance(policy.get("windows"), dict) and isinstance(policy.get("defaults"), dict)
   179	             and isinstance(policy.get("accounts"), dict),
   180	             f"{path}: windows, defaults and accounts must be objects")
   181	    for key in ("counter_window_s", "measured_hold_s", "probe_timeout_s"):
   182	        _int(policy["windows"].get(key), f"{path}: windows.{key}", minimum=1)
   183	    _check_knobs(policy["defaults"], f"{path}: defaults")
   184	    for name, entry in policy["accounts"].items():
   185	        _require(isinstance(entry, dict), f"{path}: accounts.{name} must be an object")
   186	        _check_knobs(knobs_for(policy, name), f"{path}: accounts.{name}")
   187	    _check_patterns(policy.get("failure_patterns"), path)
   188	    return policy

   191	def _check_knobs(entry: dict, what: str) -> None:
   192	    _int(entry.get("floor"), f"{what}.floor", minimum=0)
   193	    aimd, health = entry.get("aimd"), entry.get("health")
   194	    _require(isinstance(aimd, dict) and isinstance(health, dict),
   195	             f"{what}: aimd and health must be objects")
   196	    _int(aimd.get("increase"), f"{what}.aimd.increase", minimum=1)
   197	    _int(aimd.get("quiet_window_s"), f"{what}.aimd.quiet_window_s", minimum=1)
   198	    _require(isinstance(aimd.get("decrease"), (int, float))
   199	             and not isinstance(aimd["decrease"], bool) and 0 < float(aimd["decrease"]) < 1,
   200	             f"{what}.aimd.decrease must lie in (0, 1)")
   201	    for key in _HEALTH_KEYS:
   202	        _int(health.get(key), f"{what}.health.{key}", minimum=1)
   203	    for key in _DISABLE_KEYS:
   204	        if key in health:
   205	            _int(health[key], f"{what}.health.{key}", minimum=1)
   206	    _require(health["probe_backoff_max_s"] >= health["probe_backoff_s"],
   207	             f"{what}.health.probe_backoff_max_s must be at least probe_backoff_s")

   210	def _check_patterns(patterns: Any, path: Path) -> None:
   211	    _require(isinstance(patterns, list) and patterns,
   212	             f"{path}: failure_patterns must be a non-empty array")
   213	    seen: set[str] = set()
   214	    for index, entry in enumerate(patterns):
   215	        where = f"{path}: failure_patterns[{index}]"
   216	        _require(isinstance(entry, dict), f"{where} must be an object")
   217	        _require(isinstance(entry.get("failure_class"), str) and entry["failure_class"]
   218	                 and entry["failure_class"] not in seen,
   219	                 f"{where}.failure_class must be a unique non-empty string")
   220	        seen.add(entry["failure_class"])
   221	        _require(entry.get("counts_as") in _COUNTS_AS,
   222	                 f"{where}.counts_as must be one of {_COUNTS_AS}")
   223	        _require(isinstance(entry.get("patterns"), list)
   224	                 and all(isinstance(item, str) for item in entry["patterns"]),
   225	                 f"{where}.patterns must be an array of strings")
   226	    _require("unknown" in seen, f"{path}: failure_patterns must define the 'unknown' class")

   252	def disabling_classes(policy: dict) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   253	    """Failure classes that disable the key outright, not just count against it.
   254	
   255	    A concurrency refusal says "too many at once"; ``auth`` and
   256	    ``insufficient_balance`` say "this key does not work at all", and no amount

   262	    return tuple(entry["failure_class"] for entry in policy["failure_patterns"]
   263	                 if entry.get("disables") and entry["failure_class"] != "endpoint_5xx")

   266	def load_run_mode(path: Path | None = None) -> dict:
   267	    """Read and validate ``watchdog/run-mode.json`` (``run_mode.py`` writes it).
   268	
   269	    Only the fields consumed here are validated, and the account list is accepted
   270	    both as the brief's array and as a name-keyed object.  A missing or malformed
   271	    file is a hard failure: never "zero capacity" and never "unlimited".
   272	    """
   273	    path = path or _env_path("MIPSTARRE_RUN_MODE", watchdog_dir() / "run-mode.json")
   274	    try:
   275	        mode = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   276	    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
   277	        raise ControllerError(f"{path}: run mode is missing or unreadable ({exc}); apply the "
   278	                              "owner's brief first: run_mode.py apply --brief PATH") from exc
   279	    _require(isinstance(mode, dict), f"{path}: run mode must be an object")
   280	    raw = mode.get("accounts")
   281	    if isinstance(raw, dict):
   282	        entries = [dict(value, name=value.get("name", key)) for key, value in raw.items()
   283	                   if isinstance(value, dict)]
   284	        _require(len(entries) == len(raw), f"{path}: every account must be an object")
   285	    else:
   286	        _require(isinstance(raw, list) and raw, f"{path}: accounts must be a non-empty array")
   287	        entries = list(raw)
   288	    accounts: dict[str, dict] = {}
   289	    for entry in entries:
   290	        _require(isinstance(entry, dict), f"{path}: every account must be an object")
   291	        name = entry.get("name")
   292	        _require(isinstance(name, str) and name and name not in accounts,
   293	                 f"{path}: account name must be a unique non-empty string, got {name!r}")
   294	        nominal = _int(entry.get("nominal_limit"), f"{path}: {name}.nominal_limit", minimum=0)
   295	        reserved = _int(entry.get("external_reserved"), f"{path}: {name}.external_reserved",
   296	                        minimum=0)
   297	        _require(reserved <= nominal,
   298	                 f"{path}: {name}.external_reserved ({reserved}) exceeds nominal_limit ({nominal})")
   299	        _require(isinstance(entry.get("enabled", True), bool),
   300	                 f"{path}: {name}.enabled must be true or false")
   301	        _require(isinstance(entry.get("endpoint") or name, str),
   302	                 f"{path}: {name}.endpoint must be a string")
   303	        accounts[name] = {"name": name, "endpoint": entry.get("endpoint") or name,
   304	                          "label": entry.get("label") or "", "nominal_limit": nominal,
   305	                          "codex_home": entry.get("codex_home") or "",
   306	                          "external_reserved": reserved, "enabled": entry.get("enabled", True)}
   307	    _require(bool(accounts), f"{path}: the brief must name at least one account")
   308	    run = mode.get("run") if isinstance(mode.get("run"), dict) else {}
   309	    accounts, source = overlay_live_accounts(accounts)
   310	    return {"accounts": accounts, "run": run, "accounts_source": source,
   311	            "brief_ref": (mode.get("brief_sha256") or mode.get("brief_ref")
   312	                          or run.get("label") or str(path))}

   315	def overlay_live_accounts(from_mode: dict[str, dict]) -> tuple[dict[str, dict], str]:
   316	    """Replace the mode's account list with the owner's live file when it exists.
   317	
   318	    THE HOT RELOAD.  ``load_run_mode`` runs once per tick, so the ceilings, the
   319	    reserved slots and the enabled flags the controller uses are at most one tick
   320	    (60 s) old.  The live file is authoritative in full: an entry the owner
   321	    removed is gone from the tick that follows, which is cap 0 and no probe —
   322	    the same as ``enabled: false``, and deliberately so.
   323	
   324	    An unreadable or invalid file is a HARD failure, like a malformed run mode:
   325	    the caller exits nonzero and leaves the cap files exactly as they are.
   326	    Falling back to the brief would silently restore a ceiling the owner has just
   327	    lowered, which is the one behaviour this file exists to remove.
   328	    """
   329	    try:
   330	        entries = accounts_file.load()
   331	    except accounts_file.AccountsError as exc:
   332	        raise ControllerError(
   333	            f"{exc}\nThe cap files are untouched. Fix the field this message names "
   334	            f"(results/telemetry/owner-tools/accounts.sh list), or delete "
   335	            f"{accounts_file.accounts_path()} to fall back to the brief.") from exc
   336	    if entries is None:
   337	        return from_mode, "run-mode.json (no accounts.json yet)"
   338	    live: dict[str, dict] = {}
   339	    for entry in entries:
   340	        name = entry["name"]
   341	        ceiling = entry["ceiling"]
   342	        reserved = min(entry["external_reserved"], ceiling)
   343	        live[name] = {"name": name, "endpoint": entry["endpoint"],
   344	                      "label": entry["label"], "nominal_limit": ceiling,
   345	                      "codex_home": entry["codex_home"],
   346	                      "external_reserved": reserved, "enabled": entry["enabled"],
   347	                      "note": entry["note"]}
   348	    _require(bool(live), f"{accounts_file.accounts_path()}: no account entries")
   349	    return live, str(accounts_file.accounts_path())

   374	def read_session_rows(path: Path, since: datetime, *, tail_bytes: int = TAIL_BYTES) -> list[dict]:
   375	    """Rows newer than *since* from the tail of ``sessions.jsonl``.
   376	
   377	    The registry grows for the life of the project and the counters never look
   378	    back further than five minutes.  A malformed row is skipped, not fatal.
   379	    """
   380	    try:
   380	    try:
   381	        size = path.stat().st_size
   382	        with path.open("rb") as handle:
   383	            if size > tail_bytes:
   384	                handle.seek(size - tail_bytes)
   385	                handle.readline()  # drop the partial row the seek landed inside
   386	            blob = handle.read()
   387	    except OSError:
   388	        return []
   389	    rows = []
   390	    for line in blob.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
   391	        try:
   392	            row = json.loads(line)
   393	        except ValueError:
   394	            continue
   395	        if not isinstance(row, dict):
   396	            continue
   397	        moment = parse_ts(row.get("end")) or parse_ts(row.get("start")) or parse_ts(row.get("ts"))
   398	        if moment is not None and moment >= since:
   399	            rows.append(dict(row, _ts=moment))
   400	    return rows

   403	def attribution_map(accounts: dict[str, dict]) -> tuple[dict[str, str], list[str]]:
   404	    """``token -> account`` for failure attribution, plus the ambiguous tokens.
   405	
   406	    Account NAMES are unique by construction and always map to themselves.  An
   407	    endpoint or a label may legitimately be shared — the owner's topology is one
   408	    to three endpoints with one or two keys on each — and a shared token cannot
   409	    say which key refused, so it is DROPPED rather than resolved to the last
   410	    entry that claimed it.  Dropping it costs nothing: every row the dispatcher
   411	    writes carries ``account``, which `observe` now reads first.  Keeping it was
   412	    an active harm — it moved a refusal, and at ``disable_threshold`` 1 a whole
   413	    key, onto a key that had done nothing.
   414	    """
   415	    endpoints: dict[str, str] = {name: name for name in accounts}
   416	    claimed: dict[str, str] = {}
   417	    ambiguous: set[str] = set()
   418	    for name, entry in accounts.items():
   419	        for token in (entry.get("endpoint"), entry.get("label")):
   420	            if not isinstance(token, str) or not token or token in endpoints:
   421	                continue  # an account name always outranks another key's label
   422	            if claimed.setdefault(token, name) != name:
   423	                ambiguous.add(token)
   424	    endpoints.update({token: owner for token, owner in claimed.items()
   425	                      if token not in ambiguous})
   426	    return endpoints, sorted(ambiguous)

   429	def observe(rows: list[dict], name: str, endpoints: dict[str, str], roles: dict[str, str],
   430	            now: datetime, *, counter_window_s: int, fivexx_window_s: int,
   431	            disabling: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> dict:
   432	    """Refusal, death and key-invalidating counters for one account.
   433	
   434	    A ``failure_class`` the policy does not name — including the literal
   435	    ``unknown`` — is counted in neither direction, so a reworded provider message
   436	    leaves the cap where a hand-set cap would have been instead of collapsing it.
   437	
   438	    ``disabling`` names the classes that say the KEY is unusable rather than busy
   439	    (``auth``, ``insufficient_balance``).  They are collected separately, with
   440	    their detail, because the answer to them is "disable this key and say why",
   441	    not "lower the cap by a quarter".
   442	    """
   443	    bucket: dict[str, Any] = {"refusals": 0, "deaths": 0, "neutral": 0,
   444	                              "deaths_by_class": {}, "refusal_times": [], "fivexx_times": [],
   445	                              "disable_times": [], "disable_class": "", "disable_detail": ""}
   446	    counter_since = now - timedelta(seconds=counter_window_s)
   447	    fivexx_since = now - timedelta(seconds=fivexx_window_s)
   448	    for row in rows:
   449	        # ``account`` FIRST.  The dispatcher writes the name it actually routed
   450	        # to; an endpoint is shared by up to two keys in the owner's own topology
   451	        # (one to three endpoints, one or two keys each).  Matching the endpoint
   452	        # first attributed a refusal to whichever key happened to be written into
   453	        # the endpoint map last, so AIMD cut the innocent key while the refusing
   454	        # one crept up, and one `auth` row disabled the wrong key at threshold 1.
   455	        owner = next((endpoints[row[field]] for field in
   456	                      ("account", "endpoint", "failure_endpoint", "key_label")
   457	                      if isinstance(row.get(field), str) and row[field] in endpoints), None)
   458	        failure_class = row.get("failure_class")
   459	        if owner != name or not isinstance(failure_class, str) or not failure_class:
   460	            continue
   461	        if failure_class == "endpoint_5xx" and row["_ts"] >= fivexx_since:
   462	            bucket["fivexx_times"].append(row["_ts"])
   463	        if row["_ts"] < counter_since:
   464	            continue
   465	        if failure_class in disabling:
   466	            bucket["disable_times"].append(row["_ts"])
   467	            bucket["disable_class"] = failure_class
   468	            bucket["disable_detail"] = str(row.get("failure_detail") or "")[:120]
   469	        role = roles.get(failure_class, "neutral")
   470	        if role == "refusal":
   471	            bucket["refusals"] += 1
   472	            bucket["refusal_times"].append(row["_ts"])
   473	        elif role == "death":
   474	            bucket["deaths"] += 1
   475	            bucket["deaths_by_class"][failure_class] = \
   476	                bucket["deaths_by_class"].get(failure_class, 0) + 1
   477	        else:
   478	            bucket["neutral"] += 1
   479	    bucket["refusal_times"].sort()
   480	    bucket["fivexx_times"].sort()
   481	    bucket["disable_times"].sort()
   482	    return bucket

   535	def _write_cap_file(path: Path, value: int) -> None:
   536	    """Write one cap file, refusing anything that is not a nonneg integer.
   537	
   538	    The guard is the point: an empty or non-numeric cap file makes every dispatch
   539	    exit 4 with ``invalid literal for int()``, silently stopping all work.
   540	    """
   541	    text = f"{int(value)}\n"
   542	    _require(int(value) >= 0 and text.strip().isdecimal(),
   543	             f"{path}: refusing to write a cap that is not a nonnegative integer ({value!r})")

   547	def write_cap_files(caps: dict[str, int]) -> int:
   548	    """Write the legacy derived outputs; ``max-codex`` is mechanically the sum.
   549	
   550	    It therefore cannot disagree with the per-account files.  It is a display and
   551	    lane-parallelism value only: admission reads the per-account files
   552	    (``local/protocols/capacity.md`` §4).
   553	    """
   554	    effective = {name: int(value) for name, value in caps.items()}
   555	    directory = watchdog_dir()
   556	    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   557	    # A cap file for an account that has dropped out of the configured set is
   558	    # ZEROED, not deleted.  Deleting it would break the "never an empty read"
   559	    # property; leaving its old number is worse still, because that stale file is
   560	    # exactly what `account_router.account_names()` picks up from its
   561	    # ``max-codex-*`` glob when accounts.json is unreadable — a key the owner
   562	    # removed would go on being admitted at the ceiling it had when they removed
   563	    # it.  The two historical names keep a file unconditionally, so a reader that
   564	    # predates this layer still finds a number.
   565	    stale = sorted(path.name[len("max-codex-"):] for path in
   566	                   directory.glob("max-codex-*")
   567	                   if path.is_file() and path.name != "max-codex"
   568	                   and path.name[len("max-codex-"):] not in effective)
   569	    for name in (*DEFAULT_ACCOUNTS, *stale,
   570	                 *(name for name in effective if name not in DEFAULT_ACCOUNTS)):
   571	        _write_cap_file(directory / f"max-codex-{name}", effective.get(name, 0))
   572	    _write_cap_file(directory / "max-codex", sum(effective.values()))
   573	    return sum(effective.values())

   579	def probe_account(account: str, codex_home: str, timeout_s: int) -> bool:
   580	    """One bounded, read-only probe of *account*'s endpoint.
   581	
   582	    A health check, not a work session: read-only sandbox, no persona, no task,
   583	    no worktree write, nothing appended to ``sessions.jsonl``.  Its record is the
   584	    health file and the ``capacity`` row in ``stages.jsonl``.
   585	    ``MIPSTARRE_CAPACITY_PROBE_CMD`` replaces the command for the health tests
   586	    and for a dry run on a host without ``codex``.
   587	    """
   588	    override = os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_CAPACITY_PROBE_CMD")
   589	    command = shlex.split(override) if override else [
   590	        os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_CODEX_BIN", "codex"), "exec", "--sandbox", "read-only",
   591	        "-C", str(repo_root()), "--", "Reply with the single word: ok"]
   592	    env = dict(os.environ, MIPSTARRE_CAPACITY_PROBE=account)
   593	    if codex_home:
   594	        env["CODEX_HOME"] = str(Path(codex_home).expanduser())
   595	    try:
   596	        return subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout_s,
   597	                              env=env).returncode == 0
   598	    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
   599	        return False

   602	def _try_probe(account: str, codex_home: str, timeout_s: int) -> tuple[bool, bool]:
   603	    """``(ran, succeeded)`` — single-flight, so two ticks cannot probe at once."""
   604	    capacity_dir().mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   605	    with (capacity_dir() / f"probe-{account}.lock").open("a") as lock:
   606	        try:
   607	            fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
   608	        except OSError:
   609	            return False, False
   610	        try:
   611	            return True, probe_account(account, codex_home, timeout_s)
   612	        finally:
   613	            fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_UN)

   616	def update_health(account: str, health: dict, counters: dict, knobs: dict, now: datetime,
   617	                  *, no_probe: bool, codex_home: str, probe_timeout_s: int) -> str:
   618	    """Advance the endpoint health machine one tick; returns what it did.
   619	
   620	    Independent of AIMD in both directions: a refusal never changes health and a

620	    Independent of AIMD in both directions: a refusal never changes health and a
   621	    5xx never runs the AIMD arithmetic.
   622	
   623	    Two kinds of trip, one machine.  ``endpoint_5xx`` says the ENDPOINT is down
   624	    and needs ``fivexx_threshold`` deaths inside ``fivexx_window_s`` — a single
   625	    502 is noise.  ``auth`` and ``insufficient_balance`` say the KEY is unusable
   626	    and trip at ``disable_threshold`` (1): a `401` is not a statistic, and
   627	    retrying an invalid key at any concurrency produces nothing but dead
   628	    sessions.  Both write the REASON into the health file, because "cap 0" with
   629	    no reason is the state the owner had to diagnose by reading captures on
   630	    2026-09-12; the way back is the same half-open probe, with the key-invalid
   631	    backoff starting longer (``disable_backoff_s``) since a key does not become
   632	    valid again in thirty seconds.
   633	    """
   634	    fivexx = len(counters["fivexx_times"])
   635	    disabling = len(counters.get("disable_times") or ())
   636	    base = knobs["probe_backoff_s"]
   637	    disable_base = max(base, int(knobs.get("disable_backoff_s",
   638	                                           _DISABLE_DEFAULTS["disable_backoff_s"])))
   639	    health.update(consecutive_5xx=fivexx, key_failures=disabling, updated=ts(now))
   640	    if health["state"] != "down":
   641	        if disabling >= int(knobs.get("disable_threshold",
   642	                                      _DISABLE_DEFAULTS["disable_threshold"])):
   643	            detail = counters.get("disable_detail") or ""
   644	            health.update(state="down", since=ts(now), probes_ok=0,
   645	                          backoff_s=min(disable_base, knobs["probe_backoff_max_s"]),
   646	                          reason=f"{counters.get('disable_class') or 'key'}: "
   647	                                 f"{detail or 'the key was refused'}",
   648	                          disabled_by=counters.get("disable_class") or "key",
   649	                          next_probe_at=ts(now + timedelta(
   650	                              seconds=min(disable_base, knobs["probe_backoff_max_s"]))))
   651	            return "trip"
   652	        if fivexx >= knobs["fivexx_threshold"]:
   653	            health.update(state="down", since=ts(now), probes_ok=0, backoff_s=base,
   654	                          reason=f"endpoint_5xx: {fivexx} deaths in "
   655	                                 f"{knobs['fivexx_window_s']}s",
   656	                          disabled_by="endpoint_5xx",
   657	                          next_probe_at=ts(now + timedelta(seconds=base)))
   658	            return "trip"
   659	        if fivexx:
   660	            if health["state"] != "degraded":
   661	                health.update(state="degraded", since=ts(now),
   662	                              reason=f"endpoint_5xx: {fivexx} death(s) in "
   663	                                     f"{knobs['fivexx_window_s']}s, below the "
   664	                                     f"threshold of {knobs['fivexx_threshold']}")
   665	            return "degraded"
   666	        if health["state"] != "up":
   667	            health.update(state="up", since=ts(now), reason="")
   668	            return "clear"
   669	        return "none"
   670	    if no_probe:  # an operator hold, or a key the brief disabled
   671	        return "probe-held"
   672	    due = parse_ts(health.get("next_probe_at"))
   673	    if due is not None and now < due:
   674	        return "probe-waiting"
   675	    ran, ok = _try_probe(account, codex_home, probe_timeout_s)
   676	    if not ran:
   677	        return "probe-inflight"
   678	    if not ok:
   679	        health["probes_ok"] = 0
   680	        health["backoff_s"] = min(int(health["backoff_s"]) * 2, knobs["probe_backoff_max_s"])
   681	        health["next_probe_at"] = ts(now + timedelta(seconds=health["backoff_s"]))
   682	        return "probe-failed"
   683	    health["probes_ok"] = int(health["probes_ok"]) + 1
   684	    if health["probes_ok"] < knobs["probes_to_recover"]:
   685	        health["next_probe_at"] = ts(now + timedelta(seconds=base))
   686	        return "probe-ok"
   687	    health.update(state="up", since=ts(now), probes_ok=0, consecutive_5xx=0,
   688	                  key_failures=0, reason="", disabled_by="",
   689	                  backoff_s=base, next_probe_at=None)
   690	    return "recovered"

   694	
   695	
   696	def clamp(value: int, floor: int, ceiling: int) -> int:
   697	    """Into ``[floor, ceiling]``; the ceiling wins when the two cross."""
   698	    return max(min(floor, ceiling), min(ceiling, int(value)))
   699	
   700	
   701	def apply_aimd(account_state: dict, counters: dict, knobs: dict, live: int, now: datetime,
   702	               *, floor: int, ceiling: int) -> list[str]:
   703	    """Decrease first, so a refusal cannot be overtaken by an increase."""
   704	    notes: list[str] = []
   705	    aimd = knobs["aimd"]
   706	    window = timedelta(seconds=aimd["quiet_window_s"])
   707	    cap = int(account_state["cap"])
   708	    cursor = parse_ts(account_state.get("refusal_cursor"))
   709	    fresh = [moment for moment in counters["refusal_times"] if cursor is None or moment > cursor]
   710	    if fresh:
   711	        until = parse_ts(account_state.get("decrease_window_until"))
   712	        if until is None or now > until:
   713	            # The FIRST refusal of a window: step just under the concurrency that
   714	            # was refused.  ``live`` is sampled at the tick that observes it,
   715	            # which is the closest the controller gets to the moment of refusal —
   716	            # but when the refused sessions have already died it is 0 or 1, and a
   717	            # raw ``live - 1`` would collapse the cap to the floor and then climb
   718	            # back one slot per quiet window (an hour from 1 to 30 with the
   719	            # shipped defaults).  Fall back to what the account is KNOWN to have
   720	            # sustained before believing an instantaneous zero.
   721	            evidence = [value for value in
   722	                        (account_state.get("observed_refusal_floor"),
   723	                         account_state.get("measured_limit"))
   724	                        if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)]
   725	            basis = live if live > 1 else max([live] + evidence)
   726	            cap = max(floor, min(cap, basis - 1))
   727	            account_state["decrease_window_until"] = ts(now + window)
   728	            notes.append(f"decrease(first) live={live} basis={basis} -> {cap}")
   729	            observed = basis
   730	        else:
   731	            cap = max(floor, math.ceil(cap * float(aimd["decrease"])))
   732	            notes.append(f"decrease(x{aimd['decrease']}) -> {cap}")
   733	            observed = live
   734	        account_state.update(refusal_cursor=ts(max(fresh)), quiet_since=None)
   735	        if observed >= 1:  # a zero census is not evidence that one slot refused
   736	            seen = account_state.get("observed_refusal_floor")
   737	            account_state["observed_refusal_floor"] = (
   738	                observed if seen is None else min(int(seen), observed))
   739	    # ``live >= cap - 1`` keeps the cap honest: a cap nobody uses is not evidence
   740	    # of headroom.
   741	    if (not counters["refusals"] and not counters["deaths"]
   742	            and account_state["health"] == "up" and live >= cap - 1):
   743	        started = parse_ts(account_state.get("quiet_since"))
   744	        if started is None:
   745	            account_state["quiet_since"] = ts(now)
   746	        elif now - started >= window:
   747	            if cap < ceiling:
   748	                cap = min(ceiling, cap + int(aimd["increase"]))
   749	                notes.append(f"increase -> {cap}")
   750	            account_state["quiet_since"] = ts(now)
   751	    else:
   752	        account_state["quiet_since"] = None
   753	    account_state["cap"] = clamp(cap, floor, ceiling)
   754	    return notes
   755	
   756	
   757	def update_measurement(account_state: dict, counters: dict, live: int, now: datetime,
   758	                       *, measured_hold_s: int) -> None:
   759	    """The highest concurrency sustained *measured_hold_s* with no refusal or death."""
   760	    if counters["refusals"] or counters["deaths"]:
   761	        account_state.update(measured_since=None, measured_level=None)
   762	        return
   763	    started = parse_ts(account_state.get("measured_since"))
   764	    level = account_state.get("measured_level")
   765	    if started is None or not isinstance(level, int):
   766	        account_state.update(measured_since=ts(now), measured_level=live)
   767	        return
   768	    account_state["measured_level"] = min(int(level), live)
   769	    if now - started >= timedelta(seconds=measured_hold_s):
   770	        sustained, current = int(account_state["measured_level"]), account_state["measured_limit"]
   771	        if current is None or sustained > int(current):
   772	            account_state["measured_limit"] = sustained
   773	        account_state.update(measured_since=ts(now), measured_level=live)
   774	
   775	
   776	def refresh(account_state: dict, entry: dict, knobs: dict) -> tuple[int, int]:
   777	    """Ceiling and floor from the brief and the policy; returns ``(floor, ceiling)``."""
   778	    ceiling = max(0, entry["nominal_limit"] - entry["external_reserved"])
   779	    floor = min(int(knobs["floor"]), ceiling)
   780	    account_state.update(nominal_limit=entry["nominal_limit"], floor=floor, ceiling=ceiling,
   781	                         external_reserved=entry["external_reserved"],
   782	                         enabled=entry["enabled"], endpoint=entry["endpoint"])
   783	    return floor, ceiling

   785	
   786	def seed_cap(account_state: dict, floor: int, ceiling: int, entry: dict) -> int:
   787	    """Starting cap for a run: ``min(brief ceiling, last measured limit)``."""
   788	    if not entry["enabled"]:
   789	        return 0
   790	    measured = account_state.get("measured_limit")
   791	    return clamp(max(ceiling if measured is None else min(ceiling, int(measured)), 1),
   792	                 floor, ceiling)

   795	def tick(now: datetime, *, policy: dict, run_mode: dict, state: dict,
   796	         dry_run: bool = False) -> dict:
   797	    """One control step: health, then decrease, then increase, then the clamp."""
   798	    windows, roles = policy["windows"], class_roles(policy)
   799	    disabling = disabling_classes(policy)
   800	    hold = (capacity_dir() / "hold").exists()
   801	    paused = state.get("paused_at") is not None
   802	    accounts = run_mode["accounts"]
   803	    endpoints, ambiguous = attribution_map(accounts)
   804	    lookback = max([windows["counter_window_s"]]
   805	                   + [health_knobs(policy, name)["fivexx_window_s"] for name in accounts])
   806	    rows = read_session_rows(telemetry_dir() / "sessions.jsonl",
   807	                             now - timedelta(seconds=lookback))
   808	    live, waiters = count_live(accounts), count_waiters()
   809	    summary: dict[str, Any] = {"ts": ts(now), "hold": hold, "paused": paused,
   810	                               "waiters": waiters, "accounts": {}}
   811	    if ambiguous:
   812	        # Legal (two keys on one endpoint) but worth saying once a tick: rows
   813	        # that carry only that token are attributed to neither key.
   814	        summary["ambiguous_endpoints"] = ambiguous
   815	    caps: dict[str, int] = {}
   816	    health_rows: dict[str, dict] = {}
   817	    estimate = {"schema": "mipstarre-capacity-estimate/1", "updated": ts(now), "accounts": {}}
   818	
   819	    for name, entry in accounts.items():
   820	        knobs = knobs_for(policy, name)
   821	        hknobs = health_knobs(policy, name)
   822	        counters = observe(rows, name, endpoints, roles, now,
   823	                           counter_window_s=windows["counter_window_s"],
   824	                           fivexx_window_s=hknobs["fivexx_window_s"],
   825	                           disabling=disabling)
   826	        account_state = state["accounts"].setdefault(name, new_account_state(name))
   827	        floor, ceiling = refresh(account_state, entry, knobs)
   828	        health = load_health(name, entry["endpoint"], now, hknobs["probe_backoff_s"])
   829	        was = health["state"]
   830	        # A paused run has no daemons and spends no key: `paused` joins the hold
   831	        # and the disabled account in suppressing the probe, so a pause can never
   832	        # fire `codex exec` on the owner's keys after the deadline.
   833	        action = update_health(name, health, counters, hknobs, now,
   834	                               no_probe=hold or paused or not entry["enabled"],
   835	                               codex_home=entry["codex_home"],
   836	                               probe_timeout_s=windows["probe_timeout_s"])
   837	        account_state["health"] = health["state"]
   838	        notes: list[str] = []
   839	        if hold:
   840	            notes.append("hold: cap frozen")
   841	        elif paused or not entry["enabled"]:
   842	            # BEFORE the recovery branch: a recovering endpoint must not raise
   843	            # the cap to 1 while state.json says paused (or while the brief says
   844	            # this key is off).  Pause outranks health in both directions.
   845	            if int(account_state["cap"]) != 0:  # a note per tick would be noise
   846	                notes.append("paused: cap 0" if paused
   847	                             else "disabled in the accounts file: cap 0, no probe")
   848	            account_state.update(cap=0, quiet_since=None, decrease_window_until=None)
   849	        elif action == "trip":
   850	            account_state.update(cap=0, quiet_since=None, decrease_window_until=None)
   851	            notes.append("endpoint down: cap 0")
   852	        elif action == "recovered":
   853	            # Never back to the pre-outage cap: the endpoint that just came back
   854	            # is the last thing to hand twenty sessions.
   855	            account_state.update(cap=clamp(1, floor, ceiling), quiet_since=None,
   856	                                 decrease_window_until=None, refusal_cursor=None)
   857	            notes.append(f"endpoint recovered: cap {account_state['cap']}, AIMD climbs")
   858	        elif health["state"] == "down":
   859	            account_state["cap"] = 0
   860	        else:
   861	            notes.extend(apply_aimd(account_state, counters, knobs, live[name], now,
   862	                                    floor=floor, ceiling=ceiling))
   863	            account_state["cap"] = clamp(account_state["cap"], floor, ceiling)
   864	        update_measurement(account_state, counters, live[name], now,
   865	                           measured_hold_s=windows["measured_hold_s"])
   866	        if notes:
   867	            account_state["last_change"] = ts(now)
   868	        caps[name] = int(account_state["cap"])
   869	        measured = account_state["measured_limit"]
   870	        estimate["accounts"][name] = {
   871	            "nominal": entry["nominal_limit"], "external_reserved": entry["external_reserved"],
   872	            "cap_now": caps[name], "live": live[name], "waiters": waiters,
   873	            "refusals_5m": counters["refusals"], "deaths_5m_by_class": counters["deaths_by_class"],
   874	            "measured_limit": measured,
   875	            "observed_refusal_floor": account_state["observed_refusal_floor"],
   876	            "external_inferred": (None if measured is None else entry["nominal_limit"]
   877	                                  - entry["external_reserved"] - int(measured)),
   878	            "health": health["state"], "updated": ts(now)}
   879	        summary["accounts"][name] = {
   880	            "cap": caps[name], "live": live[name], "floor": floor, "ceiling": ceiling,
   881	            "health": health["state"], "health_was": was, "health_action": action,
   882	            "health_reason": health.get("reason") or "",
   883	            "refusals_5m": counters["refusals"], "deaths_5m": counters["deaths"],
   884	            "neutral_5m": counters["neutral"], "measured_limit": measured,
   885	            "enabled": bool(entry["enabled"]), "endpoint": entry["endpoint"],
   886	            "label": entry.get("label") or name, "note": entry.get("note") or "",
   887	            "external_reserved": entry["external_reserved"], "notes": notes}
   888	        health_rows[name] = {
   889	            "state": health["state"], "reason": health.get("reason") or "",
   890	            "disabled_by": health.get("disabled_by") or "", "since": health.get("since"),
   891	            "endpoint": entry["endpoint"], "enabled": bool(entry["enabled"]),

  1387	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
  1388	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
  1389	                                     formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
  1390	    parser.add_argument("--policy", type=Path, help="capacity policy (default: the checkout's)")

  1392	    parser.add_argument("--now", type=_moment, help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
  1393	    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
  1394	    for name, handler, help_text in (
  1395	            ("init", cmd_init, "validate the brief and seed the starting caps"),
  1396	            ("tick", cmd_tick, "one control step (the 60 s loop)"),
  1397	            ("set", cmd_set, "operator override of one account's cap"),
  1398	            ("pause", cmd_pause, "caps to 0, saving them inside state.json"),
  1399	            ("resume", cmd_resume, "restore the saved caps and re-enter AIMD"),
  1400	            ("probe", cmd_probe, "run the health probe now (owner-tools/accounts.sh probe)")):
  1401	        sub = subparsers.add_parser(name, help=help_text)
  1402	        sub.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
  1403	        if name == "probe":
  1404	            sub.add_argument("account", nargs="?", default="",
  1405	                             help="default: every configured account")
  1406	            sub.add_argument("--force", action="store_true",

  1409	        if name == "init":

  1411	                             help="discard the carried measurement as well as the run state")
  1412	        if name == "set":

  1414	            sub.add_argument("cap", type=int)
  1415	        if name == "pause":
  1416	            sub.add_argument("--reason")
  1417	        sub.set_defaults(handler=handler)
  1418	    status = subparsers.add_parser("status", help="read-only picture of the caps and health")
  1419	    group = status.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
  1420	    group.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
  1421	    group.add_argument("--brief", action="store_true", help="one line for status-snapshot.sh")
  1422	    status.set_defaults(handler=cmd_status)

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	#
     3	# Usage: local/bin/janitor.sh [--dry-run] [--pass NAME]... [--list-passes]
     4	#                             [--no-lock] [--report PATH] [--help]
     5	#
     6	# The self-repair pass.  ONE idempotent sweep, safe to run from cron or from the
     7	# merge daemon's loop, that turns every terminal state the pipeline can reach
     8	# into either a repair or a reported line.  Everything it does is selected by a
     9	# record field — a session status, a marker's reason string, a PR state, a spool
    10	# deadline — and never by a date glob or a filename digit filter.  The
    11	# 2026-09-12 recovery script globbed `*20260912*.jsonl` and matched
    12	# `/[0-9]{3}\.needs-attention$` with `-mmin -15`, so lanes below 100 and the 1xxx
    13	# lanes were never repaired and a marker missed by one poll was never picked up
    14	# again.  Nothing here has an age filter or a digit-count filter.
    15	#
    16	# The five passes, each independently guarded (one failing pass never aborts the
    17	# others; a GitHub error is reported and retried next pass, never converted into
    18	# a local success):
    19	#
    20	#   dead-sessions   results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl rows whose last status is
    21	#                   `active` and whose process is gone.  When the capture ends in
    22	#                   an exhausted reconnect, a 5xx or a concurrency refusal the
    23	#                   same role is re-dispatched on the same PR and the same head,
    24	#                   at most twice per (pr, role, head_sha), ledger
    25	#                   $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/retries.jsonl.  A capture that
    26	#                   ends cleanly is NEVER re-dispatched.  The abandoned row is
    27	#                   marked `failed` so telemetry stops showing it live.
    28	#                   This is the recovery path for the 25 reviews that were re-run
    29	#                   by hand after the 503 outage: review.sh retries only a
    30	#                   pre-model death (ended-started < 15 s and tokens 0), so a
    31	#                   reviewer that dies after twenty minutes at
    32	#                   "Reconnecting... 5/5" leaves the PR pending forever.
    33	#                   SCOPE: only a role with a re-dispatch entry point is
    34	#                   re-dispatched, and today that is `reviewer` alone
    35	#                   (review.sh, exact head, verdict supersedes).  A dead prover,
    36	#                   orc or fixer is marked `failed` with a `residue` field in
    37	#                   $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/actions.jsonl and is the owning
    38	#                   session's to re-plan; `local/bin/ready_report.py` counts
    39	#                   those rows PER ROLE into the hourly comment on the progress
    40	#                   issue, so the unrepaired remainder reaches the owner's
    41	#                   channel instead of a local log.
    42	#   parked-lanes    every $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/lanes/*.needs-attention, no digit
    43	#                   filter and no age filter.  The recorded reason is classified;
    44	#                   `merge` and `build` go to fix-lane.sh with the committed
    45	#                   brief, at most twice per lane; every other class stays parked
    46	#                   and appears in the report.
    47	#   superseded-prs  local/bin/pr_janitor.py (empty three-dot diff AND head
    48	#                   reachable from github/main; one idempotent marker comment;
    49	#                   never closes an issue).
    50	#   stale-lanes     lane state for lanes whose PR is closed or merged is deleted
    51	#                   (20 stale 1xxx lanes were left behind on 2026-09-12).
    52	#   spool-expiry    $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/capacity/spool/*.json entries past the
    53	#                   run's dispatch_cutoff are dropped, so a spool that outlives a
    54	#                   run cannot re-launch stale work.
    55	#   owner-accounts  `ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>]
    56	#                   [enabled=true|false]` comments on the owner inbox issue are
    57	#                   applied to the live accounts file and answered with one
    58	#                   `applied:` / `rejected:` reply per comment
    59	#                   (local/bin/accounts_inbox.py).  ONLY comments written by the
    60	#                   repository owner login are applied; the author check, the
    61	#                   parsing and the validation live in that tool and in
    62	#                   local/bin/accounts_file.py, never here.  It is the owner's
    63	#                   channel for a ceiling change when they are away from a
    64	#                   shell: on 2026-09-12 every such change was a message to a
    65	#                   session that had to be idle to receive it.
    66	#
    67	# The janitor repairs; it never merges, never pushes, never closes an issue and
    68	# never touches a gate.  Repairs are dispatched through fix-lane.sh ->
    69	# dispatch.sh (agents never invoke codex directly) and the lane tail is
    70	# relaunched through the repository's own local/bin/lane.sh.
    71	#
    72	# Runner: results/telemetry/owner-tools/merge-daemon.sh calls this once every
    73	# `janitor_interval_s` (daemon.conf), detached and bounded; the sweep takes its
    74	# own lock, so an overlapping call exits instead of doubling up.  Nothing else
    75	# runs it: a checkout whose merge daemon is not running has no self-repair.
    76	#

   235	# capture_class FILE -> how a captured `codex exec --json` stream ended.
   236	#   clean               a completed turn is the last event   -> never re-dispatch
   237	#   reconnect-exhausted "Reconnecting... N/N" (the retry budget ran out)

   239	#   concurrency-limit   the provider refused the session (concurrency / 429)
