   242	capture_class_builtin() {
   243	  local file="$1" last=""
   244	  [ -n "$file" ] && [ -s "$file" ] || { echo "empty"; return 0; }
   245	  last="$(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*$' "$file" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)"
   246	  # A clean end wins over anything earlier in the stream: a session that
   247	  # reconnected once and then finished its turn is not a failure.
   248	  case "$last" in
   249	    *'"type":"turn.completed"'*|*'"type": "turn.completed"'*|\
   250	    *'"type":"thread.completed"'*|*'"type": "thread.completed"'*|\
   251	    *'"type":"session.completed"'*|*'"type": "session.completed"'*|\
   252	    *'"type":"response.completed"'*|*'"type": "response.completed"'*)
   253	      echo "clean"; return 0 ;;
   254	  esac
   255	  if grep -qE 'Reconnecting\.\.\.? ([0-9]+)/\1' "$file" 2>/dev/null; then

   263	  fi
   264	  echo "unknown"
   265	}

item.text: One cross-file break is confirmed: routing and `CODEX_HOME` hot-reload from `accounts.json`, but dispatch telemetry still resolves the key label and endpoint only from the one-shot run mode. A newly added key therefore runs successfully while every session row records `unknown`, undermining the per-key reporting this PR adds.

   429	def observe(rows: list[dict], name: str, endpoints: dict[str, str], roles: dict[str, str],
   430	            now: datetime, *, counter_window_s: int, fivexx_window_s: int,
   431	            disabling: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> dict:
   432	    """Refusal, death and key-invalidating counters for one account.
   433	
   434	    A ``failure_class`` the policy does not name — including the literal
   435	    ``unknown`` — is counted in neither direction, so a reworded provider message
   436	    leaves the cap where a hand-set cap would have been instead of collapsing it.
   437	
   438	    ``disabling`` names the classes that say the KEY is unusable rather than busy
   439	    (``auth``, ``insufficient_balance``).  They are collected separately, with
   440	    their detail, because the answer to them is "disable this key and say why",
   441	    not "lower the cap by a quarter".
   442	    """
   443	    bucket: dict[str, Any] = {"refusals": 0, "deaths": 0, "neutral": 0,
   444	                              "deaths_by_class": {}, "refusal_times": [], "fivexx_times": [],
   445	                              "disable_times": [], "disable_class": "", "disable_detail": ""}
   446	    counter_since = now - timedelta(seconds=counter_window_s)
   447	    fivexx_since = now - timedelta(seconds=fivexx_window_s)
   448	    for row in rows:
   449	        # ``account`` FIRST.  The dispatcher writes the name it actually routed
   450	        # to; an endpoint is shared by up to two keys in the owner's own topology
   451	        # (one to three endpoints, one or two keys each).  Matching the endpoint
   452	        # first attributed a refusal to whichever key happened to be written into
   453	        # the endpoint map last, so AIMD cut the innocent key while the refusing
   454	        # one crept up, and one `auth` row disabled the wrong key at threshold 1.
   455	        owner = next((endpoints[row[field]] for field in
   456	                      ("account", "endpoint", "failure_endpoint", "key_label")
   457	                      if isinstance(row.get(field), str) and row[field] in endpoints), None)
   458	        failure_class = row.get("failure_class")
   459	        if owner != name or not isinstance(failure_class, str) or not failure_class:
   460	            continue
   461	        if failure_class == "endpoint_5xx" and row["_ts"] >= fivexx_since:
   462	            bucket["fivexx_times"].append(row["_ts"])
   463	        if row["_ts"] < counter_since:
   464	            continue
   465	        if failure_class in disabling:
   466	            bucket["disable_times"].append(row["_ts"])
   467	            bucket["disable_class"] = failure_class
   468	            bucket["disable_detail"] = str(row.get("failure_detail") or "")[:120]
   469	        role = roles.get(failure_class, "neutral")
   470	        if role == "refusal":
   471	            bucket["refusals"] += 1
   472	            bucket["refusal_times"].append(row["_ts"])
   473	        elif role == "death":
   474	            bucket["deaths"] += 1
   475	            bucket["deaths_by_class"][failure_class] = \
   476	                bucket["deaths_by_class"].get(failure_class, 0) + 1
   477	        else:
   478	            bucket["neutral"] += 1
   479	    bucket["refusal_times"].sort()
   480	    bucket["fivexx_times"].sort()
   481	    bucket["disable_times"].sort()

   489	def parse_directives(text: str) -> list[dict]:
   490	    """Every ``ACCOUNTS:`` line of a comment, parsed or rejected by name.
   491	
   492	    Returns one record per directive line::
   493	
   494	        {"raw": "...", "name": "second", "fields": {"ceiling": "20"}, "error": ""}
   495	
   496	    A record with a non-empty ``error`` is reported back to the owner rather than
   497	    applied, so a typo is answered instead of ignored.  Nothing outside an
   498	    ``ACCOUNTS:`` line is looked at: the rest of the comment is prose.
   499	    """

   501	    for line in (text or "").splitlines():
   502	        match = DIRECTIVE_RE.match(line)
   503	        if not match:
   504	            continue
   505	        record = {"raw": sanitize(line.strip(), 200), "name": "", "fields": {},
   506	                  "error": ""}
   507	        tokens = match.group("rest").split()
   508	        name = tokens[0] if tokens else ""

   510	            record["error"] = (f"the first word after 'ACCOUNTS:' must be an account "
   511	                               f"name matching {NAME_RE.pattern}, got {name!r}")
   512	            out.append(record)

   518	                record["error"] = (f"{token!r} is not a 'field=value' assignment; the "
   519	                                   "form is 'ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> "
   520	                                   "[reserved=<n>] [enabled=true|false]'")
   521	                break
   522	            key = assignment.group("key").lower()
   523	            if key not in DIRECTIVE_FIELDS:
   524	                record["error"] = (f"field {key!r} may not be set from a comment; this "
   525	                                   f"channel carries {', '.join(DIRECTIVE_FIELDS)} only "
   526	                                   "(an endpoint or a codex home is a path on the host "
   527	                                   "and is set with accounts.sh)")
   528	                break
   529	            record["fields"][key] = assignment.group("value")
   530	        if not record["error"] and not record["fields"]:
   531	            record["error"] = ("no field to set; the form is 'ACCOUNTS: <name> "
   532	                               "ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>] [enabled=true|false]'")

+itself with a reason and probes its own way back.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""The owner-inbox comment channel for the live accounts file.
+
+`local/bin/accounts_inbox.py` applies `ACCOUNTS:` comments on the owner inbox
+issue and answers each one.  Three properties are load-bearing and are what
+these cases check: only the repository owner's comments are applied, a comment
+is applied exactly once however often the janitor sweeps, and every directive —
+applied or rejected — is echoed back so the owner knows what took effect.
+
+`gh` is never invoked: `gh_common.api` is replaced by a fake GitHub that serves
+a comment list and records the writes.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import contextlib
+import io
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest import mock
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "local" / "bin"))
+
+import accounts_file as af  # noqa: E402
+import accounts_inbox as inbox  # noqa: E402
+
+OWNER = "Dengnifer"
+ISSUE = 500
+
+BRIEF_ROWS = [
+    {"name": "primary", "label": "relay-us7", "endpoint": "relay-us7",
+     "codex_home": "~/.codex", "nominal_limit": 5, "external_reserved": 0,
+     "enabled": True},
+    {"name": "second", "label": "space", "endpoint": "api.finite-dimensional.space",
+     "codex_home": "~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/codex-home-yxy", "nominal_limit": 30,
+     "external_reserved": 2, "enabled": True},
+]
+

+class FakeGitHub:
+    """Just enough of the REST surface: list comments, create one, patch one."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.comments: list[dict] = []
+        self.posted: list[dict] = []
+        self.next_id = 1000
+
+    def comment(self, body: str, login: str) -> int:
+        self.next_id += 1
+        self.comments.append({"id": self.next_id, "body": body,
+                              "user": {"login": login}})
+        return self.next_id
+
+    def api(self, path, *, method=None, payload=None, paginate=False,
+            mutation=False, idempotent=False, absolute=False):
+        if path.startswith(f"issues/{ISSUE}/comments") and method is None:
+            return list(self.comments)
+        if path.startswith(f"issues/{ISSUE}/comments") and method == "POST":
+            number = self.comment(payload["body"], "github-actions")
+            self.posted.append(payload)
+            return {"id": number}
+        if path.startswith("issues/comments/") and method == "PATCH":
+            self.posted.append(payload)
+            return {"id": 0}
+        raise AssertionError(f"unexpected API call {method or 'GET'} {path}")
+

+class InboxHarness(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self) -> None:
+        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
+        self.cache = Path(self.tmp.name) / "cache"
+        (self.cache / "watchdog").mkdir(parents=True)
+        environment = mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {
+            "MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT": str(self.cache),
+            "MIPSTARRE_OWNER_LOGIN": OWNER,
+        })
+        environment.start()
+        self.addCleanup(environment.stop)
+        af.seed(BRIEF_ROWS, root=self.cache, source="test")
+        self.github = FakeGitHub()
+        patched = mock.patch.object(inbox.gh_common, "api", self.github.api)
+        patched.start()
+        self.addCleanup(patched.stop)
+
+    def sweep(self, **kwargs) -> list[str]:
+        out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
+        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
+            report = inbox.sweep(ISSUE, **kwargs)
+        return report
+
+    def ceiling(self, name: str) -> int:
+        return af.load_map(self.cache)[name]["ceiling"]

+        # re-apply the comment and undo that.

+        af.save(entries, root=self.cache, actor="owner", action="set", detail="8")
+        report = self.sweep()
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 8)
+        self.assertEqual(len(self.github.posted), 1)
+        self.assertIn("no new ACCOUNTS: directive", report[0])

+        self.github.comment("Can you raise the yxy key a bit?", OWNER)
+        report = self.sweep()
+        self.assertEqual(self.github.posted, [])
+        self.assertIn("no new ACCOUNTS: directive", report[0])

+    def test_a_bad_directive_is_answered_with_the_reason(self) -> None:
+        self.github.comment("ACCOUNTS: fourth ceiling=3\n"

+        self.sweep()
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 30)
+        body = self.github.posted[0]["body"]

+        self.github.comment("ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=20\n", OWNER)

+        self.assertTrue(any("dry run" in line for line in report))

+        self.github.comment("ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=20\n", OWNER)
+        self.sweep()
+        # The reply quotes the rejected directive lines verbatim; re-reading it
+        # as input would loop the channel against itself.
+        self.github.comment("ACCOUNTS: nope ceiling=1\n", OWNER)
+        self.sweep()
+        report = self.sweep()
+        self.assertIn("no new ACCOUNTS: directive", report[0])
+
+
+class TestStaleness(InboxHarness):
+    """A directive the janitor never saw is stale capacity advice.
+
+    The count cap alone did not implement the module's own rule: the owner inbox
+    issue is permissions-only and low traffic, so every `ACCOUNTS:` comment ever
+    written stayed in scope forever.  With the pipeline deliberately paused, the
+    first sweep after a resume would have applied the whole backlog at once —
+    `enabled=false` included, which is cap 0 and no probe.
+    """
+
+    def old_comment(self, body: str, minutes: int) -> int:
+        number = self.github.comment(body, OWNER)
+        moment = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(minutes=minutes)
+        self.github.comments[-1]["created_at"] = \
+            moment.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
+        return number
+
+    def test_a_day_old_directive_is_neither_applied_nor_answered(self) -> None:
+        self.old_comment("ACCOUNTS: second enabled=false\n", 60 * 24)
+        report = self.sweep()
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 30)
+        self.assertTrue(af.load_map(self.cache)["second"]["enabled"])
+        self.assertEqual(self.github.posted, [])
+        self.assertTrue(any("NOT applied" in line for line in report))
+
+    def test_a_recent_directive_still_applies(self) -> None:
+        self.old_comment("ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=20\n", 5)
+        self.sweep()
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 20)
+        self.assertEqual(len(self.github.posted), 1)
+
+    def test_a_comment_with_no_timestamp_is_not_treated_as_stale(self) -> None:
+        # The REST API always supplies created_at; a missing one is an unusual
+        # payload, not an old comment, and dropping it would lose a real edit.
+        self.github.comment("ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=18\n", OWNER)
+        self.sweep()
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 18)
+
+    def test_the_bound_can_be_turned_off(self) -> None:
+        self.old_comment("ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=20\n", 60 * 24)
+        self.sweep(max_age_min=0)
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 20)
+
+
+class TestApplyOnce(InboxHarness):

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""N named accounts through `local/bin/account_router.py`.
+
+Two key names were hard-coded through the layer — ``ACCOUNTS = ("primary",
+"second")``, ``for account in primary second``, the ``--account`` choices — so
+the owner's third key could not be expressed at all.  These cases check the
+generalization and, just as importantly, that the two historical names keep
+behaving exactly as they did: every existing brief, cap file and session row
+must survive untouched.
+
+Nothing here contacts ghz: temporary directories, no ``gh``, no ``codex``.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest import mock
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "local" / "bin"))
+
+import account_router as ar  # noqa: E402
+import accounts_file as af  # noqa: E402
+
+
+class RouterHarness(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self) -> None:
+        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
+        self.root = Path(self.tmp.name) / "cache"
+        self.watchdog = self.root / "watchdog"
+        self.watchdog.mkdir(parents=True)
+        (self.root / "accounts").mkdir(parents=True)
+        environment = mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {
+            "MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT": str(self.root)})
+        environment.start()
+        self.addCleanup(environment.stop)
+        os.environ.pop("MIPSTARRE_CODEX_HOME_SECOND", None)
+
+    def caps(self, **values: int) -> None:
+        for name, value in values.items():
+            (self.watchdog / f"max-codex-{name}").write_text(f"{value}\n",
+                                                             encoding="utf-8")
+
+    def accounts(self, *entries: dict) -> None:
+        af.save(list(entries), root=self.root, actor="test", action="write",
+                detail="fixture")
+
+    def entry(self, name: str, ceiling: int = 10, **fields) -> dict:
+        row = {"name": name, "label": name, "endpoint": f"api.{name}.example",
+               "codex_home": str(self.root / f"codex-{name}"), "ceiling": ceiling,
+               "external_reserved": 0, "enabled": True, "note": ""}
+        row.update(fields)
+        return row
+
+    def occupy(self, account: str, count: int) -> None:
+        directory = self.root / "accounts" / account
+        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        for index in range(count):
+            # Our own pid is alive by definition, so these markers count as live
+            # without spawning anything.
+            (directory / str(os.getpid() - index if os.getpid() - index > 0
+                             else index + 1)).touch()
+
+    def health_down(self, account: str) -> None:
+        path = self.watchdog / "capacity" / f"health-{account}.json"
+        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        path.write_text(json.dumps({"state": "down", "reason": "auth: 401"}),
+                        encoding="utf-8")
+
+
+class TestAccountNames(RouterHarness):
+    def test_the_live_file_is_the_first_source(self) -> None:
+        self.accounts(self.entry("primary", 5), self.entry("second", 30),
+                      self.entry("third", 8))
+        self.assertEqual(ar.account_names(self.root), ("primary", "second", "third"))
+
+    def test_cap_files_are_the_second_source(self) -> None:
+        self.caps(primary=5, second=28, third=8)
+        self.assertEqual(ar.account_names(self.root), ("primary", "second", "third"))
+        self.assertNotIn("max-codex", ar.account_names(self.root))
+
+    def test_the_two_historical_names_are_the_last_fallback(self) -> None:
+        self.assertEqual(ar.account_names(self.root), ar.DEFAULT_ACCOUNTS)
+
+    def test_an_invalid_file_falls_through_instead_of_stopping_dispatch(self) -> None:
+        # The capacity controller reports that error loudly; admission must not
+        # stop because the owner mistyped a field.
+        (self.watchdog / "accounts.json").write_text("{oops", encoding="utf-8")
+        self.caps(primary=5, second=28)
+        self.assertEqual(ar.account_names(self.root), ("primary", "second"))
+
+    def test_homes_come_from_the_file_with_the_historical_defaults(self) -> None:
+        self.accounts(self.entry("primary", 5), self.entry("third", 8))
+        homes = ar.account_homes(self.root)
+        self.assertEqual(homes["third"], self.root / "codex-third")
+        self.assertIn("second", homes)  # the historical default survives
+
+
+class TestEffectiveCaps(RouterHarness):
+    def test_a_down_endpoint_is_zero(self) -> None:
+        self.caps(primary=5, second=28)
+        self.health_down("primary")
+        self.assertEqual(ar.effective_caps(self.root), [0, 28])
+
+    def test_an_account_the_owner_disabled_is_zero_before_the_next_tick(self) -> None:
+        # Between the owner's edit and the controller's tick — up to 60 s — the
+        # cap file still holds the old number.  Reading the file here closes the
+        # window, and can only ever narrow admission.
+        self.accounts(self.entry("primary", 5), self.entry("second", 30, enabled=False))
+        self.caps(primary=5, second=28)
+        self.assertEqual(ar.effective_caps(self.root), [5, 0])
+
+    def test_a_missing_cap_file_is_zero_not_unlimited(self) -> None:
+        self.accounts(self.entry("primary", 5), self.entry("third", 8))
+        self.caps(primary=5)
+        self.assertEqual(ar.effective_caps(self.root), [5, 0])
+
+    def test_a_name_with_no_resolvable_home_is_zero(self) -> None:
+        # The fail-open hole.  `account_names` falls back to the max-codex-*
+        # glob when the file does not parse, but `account_homes` has no such
+        # glob — so `third` was admitted while dispatch.sh could not place it
+        # and ran the worker on the ambient ~/.codex, putting cap(second) +
+        # cap(third) sessions on the owner's 5-slot primary key.
+        (self.watchdog / "accounts.json").write_text('{"cieling": 5}', encoding="utf-8")
+        self.caps(primary=5, second=30, third=8)
+        names = ar.account_names(self.root)
+        self.assertEqual(names, ("primary", "second", "third"))
+        self.assertEqual(ar.effective_caps(self.root, names), [5, 30, 0])
+
+    def test_a_homeless_name_is_never_reserved_on(self) -> None:
+        (self.watchdog / "accounts.json").write_text("{oops", encoding="utf-8")
+        self.caps(primary=0, second=0, third=8)
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            ar.reserve(self.root, "third", 4321, 0, dry_run=True)
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            ar.reserve(self.root, "auto", 4321, 0, dry_run=True)
+
+    def test_a_negative_cap_is_refused(self) -> None:
+        self.caps(primary=-1, second=1)
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            ar.effective_caps(self.root)
+
+
+class TestChooseAccount(RouterHarness):
+    def test_two_accounts_behave_exactly_as_before(self) -> None:
+        names = ("primary", "second")
+        # The historical rule was live[0]*caps[1] <= live[1]*caps[0] -> primary.
+        for live, caps, expected in (
+                ([0, 0], [5, 30], "primary"),
+                ([5, 0], [5, 30], "second"),
+                ([1, 6], [5, 30], "primary"),
+                ([2, 6], [5, 30], "second"),
+                ([1, 6], [5, 30], "primary")):
+            with self.subTest(live=live, caps=caps):
+                historical = ("primary" if live[0] * caps[1] <= live[1] * caps[0]
+                              else "second")
+                self.assertEqual(ar.choose_account(live, caps, names), expected)
+                self.assertEqual(ar.choose_account(live, caps, names), historical)
+
+    def test_the_emptiest_key_wins_across_three(self) -> None:
+        names = ("primary", "second", "third")
+        self.assertEqual(ar.choose_account([4, 3, 0], [5, 30, 8], names), "third")
+        self.assertEqual(ar.choose_account([4, 3, 7], [5, 30, 8], names), "second")
+
+    def test_a_zero_cap_is_never_chosen(self) -> None:
+        # Treating a zero cap as infinitely free is how a dead endpoint attracted
+        # every dispatch on 2026-09-12.
+        names = ("primary", "second")
+        self.assertEqual(ar.choose_account([0, 0], [0, 4], names), "second")
+
+
+class TestReserve(RouterHarness):
+    def test_a_third_account_is_reservable(self) -> None:
+        self.accounts(self.entry("primary", 5), self.entry("second", 30),
+                      self.entry("third", 8))
+        self.caps(primary=0, second=0, third=2)
+        self.assertEqual(ar.reserve(self.root, "auto", 4242, 0, True), "third")
+        self.assertEqual(ar.reserve(self.root, "third", 4242, 0, True), "third")
+
+    def test_an_unconfigured_name_is_refused_by_name(self) -> None:
+        self.accounts(self.entry("primary", 5), self.entry("second", 30))
+        self.caps(primary=5, second=28)
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
+            ar.reserve(self.root, "fourth", 4242, 0, True)
+        self.assertIn("fourth", str(caught.exception))
+        self.assertIn("accounts.sh add", str(caught.exception))
+
+    def test_a_full_account_is_not_a_candidate(self) -> None:
+        self.accounts(self.entry("primary", 5), self.entry("second", 30))
+        self.caps(primary=1, second=4)
+        self.occupy("primary", 1)
+        self.assertEqual(ar.reserve(self.root, "auto", 4242, 0, True), "second")
+
+    def test_exhausted_capacity_raises_rather_than_choosing_anyway(self) -> None:
+        self.caps(primary=0, second=0)
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
+            ar.reserve(self.root, "auto", 4242, 0, True)
+        self.assertIn("capacity exhausted", str(caught.exception))
+
+    def test_drain_still_releases_a_queued_reservation(self) -> None:
+        self.accounts(self.entry("primary", 5))
+        self.caps(primary=0)
+        (self.watchdog / "drain").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
+        with self.assertRaises(ar.DrainRequested):
+            ar.reserve(self.root, "auto", 4242, 0, True)
+
+    def test_a_dry_run_reserves_nothing(self) -> None:
+        self.accounts(self.entry("primary", 5))
+        self.caps(primary=5)
+        ar.reserve(self.root, "auto", 4242, 0, True)
+        self.assertFalse((self.root / "accounts" / "primary" / "4242").exists())
+
+
+class TestAffinity(RouterHarness):
+    def test_a_retired_account_still_owns_its_thread(self) -> None:
+        # Affinity is judged on the recorded name, not on today's list: reading a
+        # historical row as "not an account" would silently turn a resume into a
+        # fresh thread.
+        self.assertTrue(ar.is_account_name("retired-key"))
+        self.assertFalse(ar.is_account_name(""))
+        self.assertFalse(ar.is_account_name("Not Valid"))
+        self.assertFalse(ar.is_account_name(None))
+
+    def test_resume_account_reads_any_valid_name(self) -> None:
+        registry = self.root / "sessions.jsonl"
+        registry.write_text(json.dumps({
+            "name": "prover-1", "thread_id": "abc", "account": "third"}) + "\n",
+            encoding="utf-8")
+        self.assertEqual(ar.resume_account("abc", registry, {}), "third")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+    """A typo in the file the owner is invited to hand-edit must not break the
+    pause.  `owner-pause.sh` phase T+0:00 is `run_mode.py pause`; when that
+    exited 2, admission was never stopped, the pre-pause caps were never saved,
+    and the whole script exited 3 — while the GitHub channel, the one remote
+    repair path for that very file, was dead for the same reason."""
+
+    def break_accounts(self) -> None:
+        path = self.cache / "watchdog" / "accounts.json"
+        document = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+        document["accounts"][0]["cieling"] = 5      # the owner's typo
+        path.write_text(json.dumps(document), encoding="utf-8")
+
+    def test_pause_still_zeroes_and_saves_the_caps(self) -> None:
+        self.assertEqual(run(["apply"])[0], 0)
+        self.break_accounts()
+        code, _, err = run(["pause", "--reason", "owner word"])
+        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
+        self.assertIn("WARNING", err)
+        self.assertIn("cieling", err)
+        self.assertEqual((self.cap("max-codex-primary"), self.cap("max-codex-second"),
+                          self.cap("max-codex")), ("0", "0", "0"))
+        self.assertEqual(self.mode()["saved_caps"], {"primary": 5, "second": 28})
+
+    def test_resume_still_restores_the_saved_caps(self) -> None:
+        self.assertEqual(run(["apply"])[0], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(run(["pause"])[0], 0)
+        self.break_accounts()
+        self.assertEqual(run(["resume"])[0], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(self.cap("max-codex-primary"), "5")
+
+    def test_a_run_scalar_is_still_answerable(self) -> None:
+        self.assertEqual(run(["apply"])[0], 0)
+        expected = run(["get", "owner_inbox_issue"])[1].strip()
+        self.break_accounts()
+        code, out, err = run(["get", "owner_inbox_issue"])
+        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
+        self.assertEqual(out.strip(), expected)
+        self.assertIn("WARNING", err)

     2	"""The owner's run briefing, validated once, and the mode file everything reads.
     3	
     4	One artifact states a run's capacity, schedule, speed and issue numbers: the
     5	brief the owner copies to ``~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/run-brief.json``
     6	from the committed template
     7	``results/telemetry/owner-tools/run-brief.template.json``.  ``apply`` validates
     8	it strictly and turns it into ``watchdog/run-mode.json``, the record every
     9	component reads through ``run_mode.py get KEY``.  No protocol, persona or
    10	script carries a literal cap, floor, cadence or issue number
    11	(``local/protocols/full-speed-mode.md``).
    12	
    13	Subcommands::
    14	
    15	    run_mode.py apply [--brief PATH] [--dry-run]
    16	    run_mode.py show [--json | --oneline]
    17	    run_mode.py get KEY
    18	    run_mode.py set speed fast|default [--dry-run]
    19	    run_mode.py pause [--reason TEXT]
    20	    run_mode.py resume
    21	
    22	``show --oneline`` renders the whole mode on one line; it is what the goal text
    23	(``owner-tools/goal-keeper.sh``) and the resume message
    24	(``owner-tools/owner-resume.sh``) carry, so neither has to name a number.
    25	
    26	``watchdog/account-mode`` is DERIVED from ``accounts[].enabled`` by ``apply``,
    27	``pause`` and ``resume`` — ``both`` when more than one account is enabled and
    28	``primary`` otherwise — because the deployed PATH shim reads it before it lets a
    29	dispatch use a second ``CODEX_HOME``.  It is not a field anyone briefs.
    30	
    31	``models.override`` is resolved against the speed tier rather than read
    32	literally: ``null`` means ``astra-all`` whenever ``run.speed`` is ``fast`` — in
    33	full speed mode every role, reviewers included, runs the hard model — and the
    34	published ``local/model-policy.json`` otherwise.  The literal ``"policy"`` keeps
    35	the published policy at any speed; ``"astra-all"`` forces the hard model at any
    36	speed.  ``set speed`` re-resolves it, so the tier and the models never disagree.
    37	
    38	Validation fails loudly at briefing time rather than at 05:00Z: an unknown
    39	key, a missing endpoint, a non-integer limit, ``external_reserved >=
    40	nominal_limit``, an occupancy target above 1, an unknown speed or model
    41	override, a non-positive issue number, or an account name outside
    42	``[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`` all exit 2 naming the offending key and the
    43	template path.  A missing brief is a hard error naming both paths — never
    44	silently zero and never silently unlimited capacity.
    45	
    46	**The brief seeds; the accounts file lives.**  ``apply`` writes
    47	``watchdog/accounts.json`` (``local/bin/accounts_file.py``) from the brief's
    48	``accounts`` block when that file does not exist, and **never overwrites an
    49	existing one**; where it exists it is what ``apply`` reads, so re-applying a
    50	brief to change the speed tier cannot undo the ceilings the owner has been
    51	editing all morning.  Any number of named accounts: ``primary`` and ``second``

   447	def resolve_override(speed: str, briefed: str | None) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
   448	    """The override actually in force for *speed*, and where it came from.
   449	
   450	    A briefed ``null`` resolves from the speed tier: ``fast`` is ``astra-all``,
   451	    because in full speed mode every role — reviewers included — runs the hard
   452	    model.  ``"policy"`` is how a fast run says "leave the published policy
   453	    alone"; it is deliberately a word rather than the absence of one, so the
   454	    file records a decision instead of an omission.

   551	def effective_caps(brief: dict, measured: dict[str, int] | None = None) -> dict[str, int]:
   552	    """Starting cap per account.
   553	
   554	    ``cap0 = clamp(1, nominal_limit - external_reserved,
   555	    last_measured_limit or nominal_limit - external_reserved)`` — a run starts
   556	    below the measured cliff instead of above it.  A disabled or unlisted
   557	    account is 0: the pipeline never dispatches there at all.
   558	    """
   559	    seen = measured or {}
   560	    caps = {account["name"]: 0 for account in brief["accounts"]}

560	    caps = {account["name"]: 0 for account in brief["accounts"]}
   561	    for account in brief["accounts"]:
   562	        if not account["enabled"]:
   563	            continue
   564	        base = account["nominal_limit"] - account["external_reserved"]
   565	        target = base
   566	        limit = seen.get(account["name"])
   567	        if isinstance(limit, int) and limit >= 0:
   568	            target = min(base, limit)
   569	        # A live entry may reach ``ceiling == external_reserved``: the admin has
   570	        # taken every slot of that key for now.  That is 0, not the floor of 1 —
   571	        # the clamp exists so a measured limit never seeds a disabled-looking
   572	        # cap, not to invent a slot the owner says is not theirs.
   573	        caps[account["name"]] = max(1, min(base, target)) if base > 0 else 0
   574	    return caps

   577	def floor_for(caps: dict[str, int], occupancy_target: float) -> int:
   578	    return int(occupancy_target * sum(caps.values()))

   581	def cap_values(caps: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, int]:
   582	    """The three derived files; `max-codex` is mechanically the sum.
   583	
   584	    Values are validated, never coerced: a string or ``None`` reaching a cap
   585	    file is the failure this refuses, so it must not be silently repaired.
   586	    """
   587	    values: dict[str, int] = {}
   588	    # The two historical names always get a file, even when the run no longer
   589	    # configures them: a reader that predates the live accounts file must find a
   590	    # number rather than an empty read, and 0 is the honest one.
   591	    for name in (*ACCOUNT_NAMES, *(name for name in caps if name not in ACCOUNT_NAMES)):
   592	        value = caps.get(name, 0)
   593	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0:
   594	            raise LayerError(f"refusing max-codex-{name}: {value!r} is not a "
   595	                             "nonnegative integer (an empty or non-numeric cap file "
   596	                             "makes every dispatch exit 4)")
   597	        values[f"max-codex-{name}"] = value
   598	    values["max-codex"] = sum(values.values())
   599	    return values

   623	def write_model_override(mode: dict, *, root: Path | None = None,
   624	                         dry_run: bool = False) -> str:
   625	    """Make the resolved ``models.override`` real: write or remove the knob.
   626	
   627	    Validating the field and exposing it through ``get model_override`` is not
   628	    the same as applying it. Until this ran, ``models.override`` was inert: the
   629	    only live overrides were the committed ``local/model-policy.json`` (a
   630	    reviewed PR, impossible mid-run) and a knob file a human typed — so "every
   631	    worker on the hard model" still cost a hand edit, the intervention the field
   632	    exists to remove.  What is written is the EFFECTIVE override
   633	    (``mode_override``), not the briefed word: a fast run with no override in
   634	    the brief still puts every role on the hard model.
   635	    """
   636	    path = (root or cache_root()) / MODEL_OVERRIDE_REL

   638	    if dry_run:

   641	    if override is None:

   646	        except OSError as exc:
   647	            raise LayerError(f"cannot remove the model override knob {path}: {exc}") from exc
   648	        return f"model override cleared ({path} removed)"
   649	    document = {"mode": override,
   650	                "set_by": f"run_mode.py, brief sha256 {mode['brief_sha256'][:12]}",
   651	                "reason": source}
   652	    atomic_write(path, json.dumps(document, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
   653	    return f"model override {override} active ({source}; runtime knob {path})"

   661	def account_mode(mode: dict) -> str:
   662	    """`both` when more than one account is enabled, `primary` otherwise.
   663	
   664	    DERIVED, never briefed.  The shim's `primary-only policy` check was a second
   665	    file holding a capacity decision: with the file absent it defaults to
   666	    `primary`, and every dispatch whose CODEX_HOME is not ~/.codex exits 4.  So a
   667	    brief that enabled `second` with a nominal_limit of 30 could dispatch nowhere
   668	    on that key while the capacity controller kept a cap of 28 and AIMD saw only
   669	    deaths — the idle-slot failure of 2026-09-12 intervention 2, with no message
   670	    anywhere saying why.  `accounts[].enabled` is the ONE place that decision
   671	    lives (full-speed-mode.md section 1: every number the owner states lives in
   672	    exactly one file), and this function is the only thing that derives the file
   673	    from it.
   674	    """
   675	    enabled = [a for a in mode.get("accounts", []) if a.get("enabled")]
   676	    return "both" if len(enabled) > 1 else "primary"

   758	def load_mode(root: Path | None = None, *, strict_accounts: bool = True) -> dict:
   759	    """The mode record, or ``LayerError`` — an unreadable mode is unknown.
   760	
   761	    ``strict_accounts=False`` keeps an INVALID accounts file from taking the
   762	    caller down with it.  It is for commands that can only ever narrow capacity
   763	    or that touch no ceiling at all: `pause` zeroes every cap file it finds, so a
   764	    stale name list cannot widen anything, and `get owner_inbox_issue` is how the
   765	    owner's remote repair path finds the issue to repair the file from.  Before
   766	    this, one mistyped field in the file the owner is invited to hand-edit made
   767	    `run_mode.py pause` exit 2 — so `owner-pause.sh` failed at T+0:00, admission
   768	    was never stopped, the pre-pause caps were never saved — and took the GitHub
   769	    channel down with it, exactly when the file needed remote repair.
   770	    """
   771	    path = (root or cache_root()) / "watchdog" / "run-mode.json"
   772	    try:
   773	        doc = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   774	    except FileNotFoundError as exc:

   810	    and ``resume`` would all quote the ceilings of the briefing while the
   811	    controller admitted against the ones the owner edited an hour ago — the
   812	    exact class of defect this whole layer exists to remove (the 2026-09-12

   815	    it gets a cap file, a `cap.<name>` accessor and a line in every report.

   821	    ceiling (see `load_mode`).

   833	            "field named above with results/telemetry/owner-tools/accounts.sh.\n")

  1024	def render_shim(template: str, speed: str) -> str:
  1025	    """The deployed shim for *speed*, rendered from the committed template."""
  1026	    if speed not in SPEEDS:
  1027	        raise LayerError(f"speed must be one of {SPEEDS}, got {speed!r}")
  1028	    # Position 1, the one the committed template actually uses: a single
  1029	    # anchored SPEED_ARGS= line.  Anchored at the start of the line on purpose -
  1030	    # the template's header documents both renderings, and a comment that merely
  1031	    # shows the line must never be rewritten with it.
  1032	    speed_lines = _SPEED_ARGS_RE.findall(template)
  1033	    if speed_lines:
  1034	        if len(speed_lines) != 1:
  1035	            raise LayerError(
  1036	                f"{shim_template_path()} has {len(speed_lines)} lines starting "
  1037	                "with SPEED_ARGS=; exactly one is required (install.sh renders "
  1038	                "the same line and exits 5 on the same condition).")
  1039	        return _SPEED_ARGS_RE.sub(
  1040	            lambda _match: SPEED_ARGS_LINE[speed], template, count=1)
  1041	    stripped = _SERVICE_TIER_RE.sub("", template)
  1042	    if SPEED_PLACEHOLDER in stripped:
  1043	        return _PLACEHOLDER_RE.sub(PRIORITY_ARG + " " if speed == "fast" else "", stripped)
  1044	    if SHIM_ANCHOR not in stripped:
  1045	        raise LayerError(
  1046	            f"{shim_template_path()} carries neither {SPEED_PLACEHOLDER} nor the "
  1047	            f"anchor {SHIM_ANCHOR}; the speed tier has no rendering position. Fix the "
  1048	            "committed template (results/telemetry/owner-tools/owner-bin-codex) rather "
  1049	            "than hand-patching the deployed shim.")

  1055	def record_shim() -> str:
  1056	    """Re-record the regenerated shim in ``owner-bin/manifest.sha256``.
  1057	
  1058	    ``install.sh`` releases both renderings into ``manifest.accepted`` but keeps
  1059	    ``manifest.sha256`` at the deployed one, and the merge daemon's start gate is
  1060	    ``install.sh --verify``.  Without this step the first ``set speed`` of a run
  1061	    makes the daemon refuse to start.  Best effort: a missing or failing
  1062	    installer is a warning, never a reason to leave the speed change unmade.
  1063	    """
  1064	    installer = repo_root() / "results" / "telemetry" / "owner-tools" / "install.sh"
  1065	    if not installer.is_file():
  1066	        return f"manifest not re-recorded: no {installer}"
  1067	    try:
  1068	        done = subprocess.run(["bash", str(installer), "--record", "codex"],
  1069	                              capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
  1070	    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
  1071	        return f"warning: install.sh --record codex did not run: {exc}"
  1072	    if done.returncode != 0:
  1073	        detail = (done.stderr or done.stdout).strip().splitlines()
  1074	        return ("warning: install.sh --record codex failed: "
  1075	                + (detail[-1] if detail else f"exit {done.returncode}"))
  1076	    return "manifest re-recorded (install.sh --record codex)"

  1085	def apply_speed(mode: dict, speed: str, *, dry_run: bool = False) -> str:
  1086	    """Regenerate the deployed shim; refuse when it was hand-edited."""
  1087	    template_file = shim_template_path()
  1088	    try:
  1089	        template = template_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
  1090	    except OSError as exc:
  1091	        raise LayerError(f"cannot read the shim template {template_file}: {exc}") from exc
  1092	    wanted = render_shim(template, speed)
  1093	    renderings = {render_shim(template, tier) for tier in SPEEDS}
  1094	    live_file = shim_path()
  1095	    try:
  1096	        live = live_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
  1097	    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
  1098	        raise Refused(
  1099	            f"no deployed shim at {live_file}; install the operator tools first "
  1100	            "(results/telemetry/owner-tools/install.sh)") from exc
  1101	    if live not in renderings:
  1102	        raise Refused(
  1103	            f"the deployed shim {live_file} differs from every rendering of "
  1104	            f"{template_file}; refusing to discard an emergency hand-edit.\n"
  1105	            "Fold the edit into the committed template, redeploy, then retry.\n"
  1106	            + _shim_diff(live, wanted))
  1107	    if dry_run:
  1108	        return "dry-run: shim unchanged"
  1109	    if live == wanted:
  1110	        return f"shim already at {speed} speed"
  1111	    mode_bits = os.stat(live_file).st_mode & 0o777
  1112	    atomic_write(live_file, wanted)
  1113	    os.chmod(live_file, mode_bits or 0o755)
  1114	    return f"shim regenerated at {speed} speed; {record_shim()}"

  1121	def locked_append(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
  1122	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  1123	    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o644)
  1124	    with os.fdopen(fd, "r+", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
  1125	        fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
  1126	        try:
  1127	            handle.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
  1128	            if handle.tell():
  1129	                handle.seek(handle.tell() - 1)
  1130	                if handle.read(1) != "\n":
  1131	                    handle.write("\n")
  1132	                handle.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
  1133	            handle.write(text if text.endswith("\n") else text + "\n")
  1134	            handle.flush()
  1135	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
  1136	        finally:
  1137	            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)

    20	# What it edits: ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/accounts.json, the live source of
    21	# truth for which keys exist, what their CEILINGS are, and whether the pipeline may
    22	# use them.  The capacity controller and account_router.py re-read that file every
    23	# tick and every reservation, so a change here reaches admission within 60 seconds
    24	# with no session prompted, no brief re-applied and nothing restarted.
    25	#
    26	# `ceiling` is a ceiling and never a target: the controller's AIMD discovery runs
    27	# below it and may never exceed `ceiling - external_reserved`.  Lowering it takes
    28	# effect at the next tick; raising it lets the additive creep continue.
    29	# `enabled false` is cap 0 immediately and no probes, and so is `remove`.
    30	#
    31	# Raising a ceiling is a PERMISSION, not a jump: AIMD then creeps +1 per quiet
    32	# window (120 s by default) and only while the key is saturated, so ten recovered
    33	# slots take twenty minutes of real demand.  `accounts.sh cap <name> <n>` is the

     5	# run from the checkout (which is mid-merge for minutes at a time).  They are therefore
     6	# COPIED to ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/ by this installer and never edited on the
     7	# host: on 2026-09-12 three versions of the lane runner ran at once, `merge-daemon-v9h.sh`

     9	# `assert old in s` here-doc against a 90-character substring.
    10	#
    11	# Usage:
    12	#   install.sh [--force] [--compat-tmp] [--crons] [--start-loops] [--dry-run]
    13	#   install.sh --verify                 # dependency/hash check (the merge daemon's gate)
    14	#   install.sh --record <name>          # re-record a regenerated file (run_mode.py set speed)
    15	#
    16	# Options:
    17	#   --force        overwrite a deployed copy whose hash matches no released version.
    18	#                  The previous copy is MOVED to owner-bin/attic/<ts>/, never deleted.
    19	#   --start-loops  start capacityd.sh (the 60 s capacity controller loop) if it is not
    20	#                  already running and no stop file holds it.  Without a running
    21	#                  controller nothing writes watchdog/max-codex-*, the caps stay frozen

    28	#                  a historical /tmp path runs versioned code.  Nothing is ever written or
    29	#                  edited in /tmp; an existing regular file there is refused, not clobbered.
    30	#   --crons        run install-crons.sh afterwards (crontab regenerated from run-mode).
    31	#   --dry-run      print the plan and touch nothing (implies --dry-run for --crons too).
    32	#   --dest DIR     install into DIR instead of $MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT/owner-bin (tests).

   157	# --- the PATH shim is GENERATED, not copied ---------------------------------------------
   158	# run_mode.py set speed regenerates the deployed shim from the same template by rewriting
   159	# its one SPEED_ARGS= line, so both renderings are released versions of `codex`.  The
   160	# rewrite is ANCHORED at the start of the line: the template documents both renderings in
   161	# its header, and a comment that merely shows the line must never be rewritten with it.
   162	SPEED_MARK='# @speed-args@ regenerated by run_mode.py set speed; do not edit by hand'
   163	render_shim() { # render_shim <fast|default> <src> <out>
   164	  local speed="$1" src="$2" out="$3" line n
   165	  case "$speed" in
   166	    fast) line="SPEED_ARGS=(-c 'service_tier=\"priority\"')   $SPEED_MARK" ;;
   167	    *)    line="SPEED_ARGS=()   $SPEED_MARK" ;;
   168	  esac
   169	  n="$(grep -c '^SPEED_ARGS=' "$src" || true)"
   170	  if [ "$n" != 1 ]; then
   171	    echo "$PROG: $src has $n lines starting with SPEED_ARGS=; exactly one is required" >&2
   172	    exit 5
   173	  fi
   174	  awk -v repl="$line" '
   175	    /^SPEED_ARGS=/ { print repl; next } { print }' "$src" > "$out"
   176	}

  1254	def seed_accounts(brief: dict, digest: str, source: Path, *,
  1255	                  dry_run: bool = False) -> str:
  1256	    """Write ``watchdog/accounts.json`` from the brief, only when it is absent.
  1257	
  1258	    The brief is ONE-SHOT and the accounts file is LIVE.  A brief re-applied
  1259	    mid-run — to change the speed tier, the cutoff or an issue number — must not
  1260	    undo an hour of the owner's ceiling edits, so an existing file is left
  1261	    exactly as it is and this says so.  The owner's own tools
  1262	    (``owner-tools/accounts.sh``, the ``ACCOUNTS:`` inbox comment) are the way
  1263	    it changes afterwards; ``rm`` it and re-apply to go back to the brief.
  1264	    """

  1266	    if path.exists():
  1267	        return f"{path} kept (the live accounts file is the owner's; the brief seeds it once)"

  1270	                ", ".join(f"{a['name']}={a['nominal_limit']}" for a in brief["accounts"]))
  1271	    try:
  1272	        written, path = accounts_file.seed(
  1273	            brief["accounts"], source=f"seeded from {source} sha256 {digest[:12]}")
  1274	    except accounts_file.AccountsError as exc:
  1275	        raise BriefError("accounts", f"cannot seed {path}: {exc}") from exc
  1276	    return f"{path} {'seeded from the brief' if written else 'kept'}"

 def read_session_rows(path: Path, since: datetime, *, tail_bytes: int = TAIL_BYTES) -> list[dict]:
     """Rows newer than *since* from the tail of ``sessions.jsonl``.
 
     The registry grows for the life of the project and the counters never look
     back further than five minutes.  A malformed row is skipped, not fatal.
     """
     try:
         size = path.stat().st_size
         with path.open("rb") as handle:
             if size > tail_bytes:
                 handle.seek(size - tail_bytes)
                 handle.readline()  # drop the partial row the seek landed inside
             blob = handle.read()
     except OSError:
         return []
     rows = []
     for line in blob.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
         try:
             row = json.loads(line)
         except ValueError:
             continue
         if not isinstance(row, dict):
             continue
         moment = parse_ts(row.get("end")) or parse_ts(row.get("start")) or parse_ts(row.get("ts"))
         if moment is not None and moment >= since:
             rows.append(dict(row, _ts=moment))
     return rows
 
 
+def attribution_map(accounts: dict[str, dict]) -> tuple[dict[str, str], list[str]]:
+    """``token -> account`` for failure attribution, plus the ambiguous tokens.
+
+    Account NAMES are unique by construction and always map to themselves.  An
+    endpoint or a label may legitimately be shared — the owner's topology is one
+    to three endpoints with one or two keys on each — and a shared token cannot
+    say which key refused, so it is DROPPED rather than resolved to the last
+    entry that claimed it.  Dropping it costs nothing: every row the dispatcher
+    writes carries ``account``, which `observe` now reads first.  Keeping it was
+    an active harm — it moved a refusal, and at ``disable_threshold`` 1 a whole
+    key, onto a key that had done nothing.

+    endpoints: dict[str, str] = {name: name for name in accounts}
+    claimed: dict[str, str] = {}
+    ambiguous: set[str] = set()
+    for name, entry in accounts.items():
+        for token in (entry.get("endpoint"), entry.get("label")):
+            if not isinstance(token, str) or not token or token in endpoints:
+                continue  # an account name always outranks another key's label
+            if claimed.setdefault(token, name) != name:
+                ambiguous.add(token)
+    endpoints.update({token: owner for token, owner in claimed.items()
+                      if token not in ambiguous})
+    return endpoints, sorted(ambiguous)

 def _append_jsonl(path: Path, record: dict) -> None:
     """One locked, newline-safe append."""
     path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
     fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o644)
     with os.fdopen(fd, "r+", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
         fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
         try:
             handle.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
             if handle.tell():
                 handle.seek(handle.tell() - 1)
                 if handle.read(1) != "\n":  # a previous writer died mid-line
                     handle.write("\n")
             handle.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
             handle.flush()
             os.fsync(handle.fileno())
         finally:
             fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)

   268	
   269	    Only the fields consumed here are validated, and the account list is accepted
   270	    both as the brief's array and as a name-keyed object.  A missing or malformed
   271	    file is a hard failure: never "zero capacity" and never "unlimited".
   272	    """

   277	        raise ControllerError(f"{path}: run mode is missing or unreadable ({exc}); apply the "
   278	                              "owner's brief first: run_mode.py apply --brief PATH") from exc
   279	    _require(isinstance(mode, dict), f"{path}: run mode must be an object")
   280	    raw = mode.get("accounts")
   281	    if isinstance(raw, dict):
   282	        entries = [dict(value, name=value.get("name", key)) for key, value in raw.items()
   283	                   if isinstance(value, dict)]

   289	    for entry in entries:
   290	        _require(isinstance(entry, dict), f"{path}: every account must be an object")

   293	                 f"{path}: account name must be a unique non-empty string, got {name!r}")

   295	        reserved = _int(entry.get("external_reserved"), f"{path}: {name}.external_reserved",
   296	                        minimum=0)
   297	        _require(reserved <= nominal,
   298	                 f"{path}: {name}.external_reserved ({reserved}) exceeds nominal_limit ({nominal})")
   299	        _require(isinstance(entry.get("enabled", True), bool),
   300	                 f"{path}: {name}.enabled must be true or false")
   301	        _require(isinstance(entry.get("endpoint") or name, str),

   306	                          "external_reserved": reserved, "enabled": entry.get("enabled", True)}
   307	    _require(bool(accounts), f"{path}: the brief must name at least one account")

   315	def overlay_live_accounts(from_mode: dict[str, dict]) -> tuple[dict[str, dict], str]:
   316	    """Replace the mode's account list with the owner's live file when it exists.
   317	
   318	    THE HOT RELOAD.  ``load_run_mode`` runs once per tick, so the ceilings, the
   319	    reserved slots and the enabled flags the controller uses are at most one tick
   320	    (60 s) old.  The live file is authoritative in full: an entry the owner
   321	    removed is gone from the tick that follows, which is cap 0 and no probe —
   322	    the same as ``enabled: false``, and deliberately so.
   323	
   324	    An unreadable or invalid file is a HARD failure, like a malformed run mode:
   325	    the caller exits nonzero and leaves the cap files exactly as they are.
   326	    Falling back to the brief would silently restore a ceiling the owner has just
   327	    lowered, which is the one behaviour this file exists to remove.
   328	    """
   329	    try:
   330	        entries = accounts_file.load()
   331	    except accounts_file.AccountsError as exc:
   332	        raise ControllerError(
   333	            f"{exc}\nThe cap files are untouched. Fix the field this message names "
   334	            f"(results/telemetry/owner-tools/accounts.sh list), or delete "
   335	            f"{accounts_file.accounts_path()} to fall back to the brief.") from exc
   336	    if entries is None:
   337	        return from_mode, "run-mode.json (no accounts.json yet)"
   338	    live: dict[str, dict] = {}
   339	    for entry in entries:
   340	        name = entry["name"]
   341	        ceiling = entry["ceiling"]
   342	        reserved = min(entry["external_reserved"], ceiling)
   343	        live[name] = {"name": name, "endpoint": entry["endpoint"],
   344	                      "label": entry["label"], "nominal_limit": ceiling,
   345	                      "codex_home": entry["codex_home"],
   346	                      "external_reserved": reserved, "enabled": entry["enabled"],
   347	                      "note": entry["note"]}
   348	    _require(bool(live), f"{accounts_file.accounts_path()}: no account entries")
   349	    return live, str(accounts_file.accounts_path())

   374	def read_session_rows(path: Path, since: datetime, *, tail_bytes: int = TAIL_BYTES) -> list[dict]:
   375	    """Rows newer than *since* from the tail of ``sessions.jsonl``.
   376	
   377	    The registry grows for the life of the project and the counters never look
   378	    back further than five minutes.  A malformed row is skipped, not fatal.
   379	    """
   380	    try:
   381	        size = path.stat().st_size
   382	        with path.open("rb") as handle:
   383	            if size > tail_bytes:
   384	                handle.seek(size - tail_bytes)
   385	                handle.readline()  # drop the partial row the seek landed inside
   386	            blob = handle.read()
   387	    except OSError:
   388	        return []
   389	    rows = []
   390	    for line in blob.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
   391	        try:
   392	            row = json.loads(line)
   393	        except ValueError:
   394	            continue
   395	        if not isinstance(row, dict):
   396	            continue
   397	        moment = parse_ts(row.get("end")) or parse_ts(row.get("start")) or parse_ts(row.get("ts"))
   398	        if moment is not None and moment >= since:
   399	            rows.append(dict(row, _ts=moment))
   400	    return rows

   403	def attribution_map(accounts: dict[str, dict]) -> tuple[dict[str, str], list[str]]:
   404	    """``token -> account`` for failure attribution, plus the ambiguous tokens.
   405	
   406	    Account NAMES are unique by construction and always map to themselves.  An
   407	    endpoint or a label may legitimately be shared — the owner's topology is one
   408	    to three endpoints with one or two keys on each — and a shared token cannot
   409	    say which key refused, so it is DROPPED rather than resolved to the last
   410	    entry that claimed it.  Dropping it costs nothing: every row the dispatcher
   411	    writes carries ``account``, which `observe` now reads first.  Keeping it was
   412	    an active harm — it moved a refusal, and at ``disable_threshold`` 1 a whole
   413	    key, onto a key that had done nothing.
   414	    """
   415	    endpoints: dict[str, str] = {name: name for name in accounts}
   416	    claimed: dict[str, str] = {}
   417	    ambiguous: set[str] = set()
   418	    for name, entry in accounts.items():
   419	        for token in (entry.get("endpoint"), entry.get("label")):
   420	            if not isinstance(token, str) or not token or token in endpoints:
   421	                continue  # an account name always outranks another key's label
   422	            if claimed.setdefault(token, name) != name:
   423	                ambiguous.add(token)
   424	    endpoints.update({token: owner for token, owner in claimed.items()
   425	                      if token not in ambiguous})
   426	    return endpoints, sorted(ambiguous)

   547	def write_cap_files(caps: dict[str, int]) -> int:
   548	    """Write the legacy derived outputs; ``max-codex`` is mechanically the sum.
   549	
   550	    It therefore cannot disagree with the per-account files.  It is a display and
   551	    lane-parallelism value only: admission reads the per-account files
   552	    (``local/protocols/capacity.md`` §4).
   553	    """
   554	    effective = {name: int(value) for name, value in caps.items()}
   555	    directory = watchdog_dir()
   556	    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   557	    # A cap file for an account that has dropped out of the configured set is
   558	    # ZEROED, not deleted.  Deleting it would break the "never an empty read"
   559	    # property; leaving its old number is worse still, because that stale file is
   560	    # exactly what `account_router.account_names()` picks up from its
   561	    # ``max-codex-*`` glob when accounts.json is unreadable — a key the owner
   562	    # removed would go on being admitted at the ceiling it had when they removed
   563	    # it.  The two historical names keep a file unconditionally, so a reader that
   564	    # predates this layer still finds a number.
   565	    stale = sorted(path.name[len("max-codex-"):] for path in
   566	                   directory.glob("max-codex-*")
   567	                   if path.is_file() and path.name != "max-codex"
   568	                   and path.name[len("max-codex-"):] not in effective)
   569	    for name in (*DEFAULT_ACCOUNTS, *stale,
   570	                 *(name for name in effective if name not in DEFAULT_ACCOUNTS)):
   571	        _write_cap_file(directory / f"max-codex-{name}", effective.get(name, 0))
   572	    _write_cap_file(directory / "max-codex", sum(effective.values()))
   573	    return sum(effective.values())

   616	def update_health(account: str, health: dict, counters: dict, knobs: dict, now: datetime,
   617	                  *, no_probe: bool, codex_home: str, probe_timeout_s: int) -> str:
   618	    """Advance the endpoint health machine one tick; returns what it did.
   619	
   620	    Independent of AIMD in both directions: a refusal never changes health and a
   621	    5xx never runs the AIMD arithmetic.
   622	
   623	    Two kinds of trip, one machine.  ``endpoint_5xx`` says the ENDPOINT is down
   624	    and needs ``fivexx_threshold`` deaths inside ``fivexx_window_s`` — a single
   625	    502 is noise.  ``auth`` and ``insufficient_balance`` say the KEY is unusable
   626	    and trip at ``disable_threshold`` (1): a `401` is not a statistic, and
   627	    retrying an invalid key at any concurrency produces nothing but dead
   628	    sessions.  Both write the REASON into the health file, because "cap 0" with
   629	    no reason is the state the owner had to diagnose by reading captures on
   630	    2026-09-12; the way back is the same half-open probe, with the key-invalid
   631	    backoff starting longer (``disable_backoff_s``) since a key does not become
   632	    valid again in thirty seconds.
   633	    """
   634	    fivexx = len(counters["fivexx_times"])
   635	    disabling = len(counters.get("disable_times") or ())
   636	    base = knobs["probe_backoff_s"]

   696	def clamp(value: int, floor: int, ceiling: int) -> int:
   697	    """Into ``[floor, ceiling]``; the ceiling wins when the two cross."""
   698	    return max(min(floor, ceiling), min(ceiling, int(value)))

   701	def apply_aimd(account_state: dict, counters: dict, knobs: dict, live: int, now: datetime,
   702	               *, floor: int, ceiling: int) -> list[str]:
   703	    """Decrease first, so a refusal cannot be overtaken by an increase."""
   704	    notes: list[str] = []
   705	    aimd = knobs["aimd"]
   706	    window = timedelta(seconds=aimd["quiet_window_s"])
   707	    cap = int(account_state["cap"])
   708	    cursor = parse_ts(account_state.get("refusal_cursor"))
   709	    fresh = [moment for moment in counters["refusal_times"] if cursor is None or moment > cursor]
   710	    if fresh:
   711	        until = parse_ts(account_state.get("decrease_window_until"))
   712	        if until is None or now > until:
   713	            # The FIRST refusal of a window: step just under the concurrency that
   714	            # was refused.  ``live`` is sampled at the tick that observes it,
   715	            # which is the closest the controller gets to the moment of refusal —
   716	            # but when the refused sessions have already died it is 0 or 1, and a
   717	            # raw ``live - 1`` would collapse the cap to the floor and then climb
   718	            # back one slot per quiet window (an hour from 1 to 30 with the
   719	            # shipped defaults).  Fall back to what the account is KNOWN to have
   720	            # sustained before believing an instantaneous zero.
   721	            evidence = [value for value in
   722	                        (account_state.get("observed_refusal_floor"),
   723	                         account_state.get("measured_limit"))
   724	                        if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)]
   725	            basis = live if live > 1 else max([live] + evidence)
   726	            cap = max(floor, min(cap, basis - 1))
   727	            account_state["decrease_window_until"] = ts(now + window)
   728	            notes.append(f"decrease(first) live={live} basis={basis} -> {cap}")
   729	            observed = basis
   730	        else:
   731	            cap = max(floor, math.ceil(cap * float(aimd["decrease"])))
   732	            notes.append(f"decrease(x{aimd['decrease']}) -> {cap}")
   733	            observed = live
   734	        account_state.update(refusal_cursor=ts(max(fresh)), quiet_since=None)
   735	        if observed >= 1:  # a zero census is not evidence that one slot refused
   736	            seen = account_state.get("observed_refusal_floor")
   737	            account_state["observed_refusal_floor"] = (
   738	                observed if seen is None else min(int(seen), observed))
   739	    # ``live >= cap - 1`` keeps the cap honest: a cap nobody uses is not evidence
   740	    # of headroom.
   741	    if (not counters["refusals"] and not counters["deaths"]
   742	            and account_state["health"] == "up" and live >= cap - 1):
   743	        started = parse_ts(account_state.get("quiet_since"))
   744	        if started is None:
   745	            account_state["quiet_since"] = ts(now)
   746	        elif now - started >= window:
   747	            if cap < ceiling:
   748	                cap = min(ceiling, cap + int(aimd["increase"]))
   749	                notes.append(f"increase -> {cap}")
   750	            account_state["quiet_since"] = ts(now)
   751	    else:
   752	        account_state["quiet_since"] = None
   753	    account_state["cap"] = clamp(cap, floor, ceiling)
   754	    return notes

   757	def update_measurement(account_state: dict, counters: dict, live: int, now: datetime,
   758	                       *, measured_hold_s: int) -> None:
   759	    """The highest concurrency sustained *measured_hold_s* with no refusal or death."""
   760	    if counters["refusals"] or counters["deaths"]:
   761	        account_state.update(measured_since=None, measured_level=None)
   762	        return
   763	    started = parse_ts(account_state.get("measured_since"))
   764	    level = account_state.get("measured_level")
   765	    if started is None or not isinstance(level, int):
   766	        account_state.update(measured_since=ts(now), measured_level=live)
   767	        return
   768	    account_state["measured_level"] = min(int(level), live)
   769	    if now - started >= timedelta(seconds=measured_hold_s):
   770	        sustained, current = int(account_state["measured_level"]), account_state["measured_limit"]
   771	        if current is None or sustained > int(current):
   772	            account_state["measured_limit"] = sustained
   773	        account_state.update(measured_since=ts(now), measured_level=live)

   776	def refresh(account_state: dict, entry: dict, knobs: dict) -> tuple[int, int]:

   778	    ceiling = max(0, entry["nominal_limit"] - entry["external_reserved"])

   795	def tick(now: datetime, *, policy: dict, run_mode: dict, state: dict,
   796	         dry_run: bool = False) -> dict:
   797	    """One control step: health, then decrease, then increase, then the clamp."""
   798	    windows, roles = policy["windows"], class_roles(policy)
   799	    disabling = disabling_classes(policy)
   800	    hold = (capacity_dir() / "hold").exists()
   801	    paused = state.get("paused_at") is not None
   802	    accounts = run_mode["accounts"]
   803	    endpoints, ambiguous = attribution_map(accounts)
   804	    lookback = max([windows["counter_window_s"]]
   805	                   + [health_knobs(policy, name)["fivexx_window_s"] for name in accounts])
   806	    rows = read_session_rows(telemetry_dir() / "sessions.jsonl",
   807	                             now - timedelta(seconds=lookback))
   808	    live, waiters = count_live(accounts), count_waiters()
   809	    summary: dict[str, Any] = {"ts": ts(now), "hold": hold, "paused": paused,
   810	                               "waiters": waiters, "accounts": {}}
   811	    if ambiguous:
   812	        # Legal (two keys on one endpoint) but worth saying once a tick: rows
   813	        # that carry only that token are attributed to neither key.
   814	        summary["ambiguous_endpoints"] = ambiguous
   815	    caps: dict[str, int] = {}
   816	    health_rows: dict[str, dict] = {}
   817	    estimate = {"schema": "mipstarre-capacity-estimate/1", "updated": ts(now), "accounts": {}}
   818	
   819	    for name, entry in accounts.items():
   820	        knobs = knobs_for(policy, name)
   821	        hknobs = health_knobs(policy, name)
   822	        counters = observe(rows, name, endpoints, roles, now,
   823	                           counter_window_s=windows["counter_window_s"],
   824	                           fivexx_window_s=hknobs["fivexx_window_s"],
   825	                           disabling=disabling)
   826	        account_state = state["accounts"].setdefault(name, new_account_state(name))
   827	        floor, ceiling = refresh(account_state, entry, knobs)
   828	        health = load_health(name, entry["endpoint"], now, hknobs["probe_backoff_s"])
   829	        was = health["state"]

   831	        # and the disabled account in suppressing the probe, so a pause can never
   832	        # fire `codex exec` on the owner's keys after the deadline.
   833	        action = update_health(name, health, counters, hknobs, now,
   834	                               no_probe=hold or paused or not entry["enabled"],
   835	                               codex_home=entry["codex_home"],
   836	                               probe_timeout_s=windows["probe_timeout_s"])
   837	        account_state["health"] = health["state"]
   838	        notes: list[str] = []
   839	        if hold:
   840	            notes.append("hold: cap frozen")
   841	        elif paused or not entry["enabled"]:
   842	            # BEFORE the recovery branch: a recovering endpoint must not raise
   843	            # the cap to 1 while state.json says paused (or while the brief says
   844	            # this key is off).  Pause outranks health in both directions.
   845	            if int(account_state["cap"]) != 0:  # a note per tick would be noise
   846	                notes.append("paused: cap 0" if paused
   847	                             else "disabled in the accounts file: cap 0, no probe")

   849	        elif action == "trip":
   850	            account_state.update(cap=0, quiet_since=None, decrease_window_until=None)
   851	            notes.append("endpoint down: cap 0")
   852	        elif action == "recovered":

   854	            # is the last thing to hand twenty sessions.
   855	            account_state.update(cap=clamp(1, floor, ceiling), quiet_since=None,
   856	                                 decrease_window_until=None, refusal_cursor=None)
   857	            notes.append(f"endpoint recovered: cap {account_state['cap']}, AIMD climbs")
   858	        elif health["state"] == "down":
   859	            account_state["cap"] = 0
   860	        else:
   861	            notes.extend(apply_aimd(account_state, counters, knobs, live[name], now,
   862	                                    floor=floor, ceiling=ceiling))
   863	            account_state["cap"] = clamp(account_state["cap"], floor, ceiling)
   864	        update_measurement(account_state, counters, live[name], now,
   865	                           measured_hold_s=windows["measured_hold_s"])
   866	        if notes:
   867	            account_state["last_change"] = ts(now)
   868	        caps[name] = int(account_state["cap"])
   869	        measured = account_state["measured_limit"]
   870	        estimate["accounts"][name] = {
   871	            "nominal": entry["nominal_limit"], "external_reserved": entry["external_reserved"],
   872	            "cap_now": caps[name], "live": live[name], "waiters": waiters,
   873	            "refusals_5m": counters["refusals"], "deaths_5m_by_class": counters["deaths_by_class"],
   874	            "measured_limit": measured,
   875	            "observed_refusal_floor": account_state["observed_refusal_floor"],
   876	            "external_inferred": (None if measured is None else entry["nominal_limit"]
   877	                                  - entry["external_reserved"] - int(measured)),
   878	            "health": health["state"], "updated": ts(now)}
   879	        summary["accounts"][name] = {
   880	            "cap": caps[name], "live": live[name], "floor": floor, "ceiling": ceiling,
   881	            "health": health["state"], "health_was": was, "health_action": action,
   882	            "health_reason": health.get("reason") or "",
   883	            "refusals_5m": counters["refusals"], "deaths_5m": counters["deaths"],
   884	            "neutral_5m": counters["neutral"], "measured_limit": measured,
   885	            "enabled": bool(entry["enabled"]), "endpoint": entry["endpoint"],
   886	            "label": entry.get("label") or name, "note": entry.get("note") or "",
   887	            "external_reserved": entry["external_reserved"], "notes": notes}

   890	            "disabled_by": health.get("disabled_by") or "", "since": health.get("since"),
   891	            "endpoint": entry["endpoint"], "enabled": bool(entry["enabled"]),
   892	            "cap": caps[name], "ceiling": ceiling,
   893	            "consecutive_5xx": health.get("consecutive_5xx", 0),
   894	            "key_failures": health.get("key_failures", 0),
   895	            "probes_ok": health.get("probes_ok", 0),
   896	            "next_probe_at": health.get("next_probe_at"),

   489	def parse_directives(text: str) -> list[dict]:
   490	    """Every ``ACCOUNTS:`` line of a comment, parsed or rejected by name.
   491	
   492	    Returns one record per directive line::
   493	
   494	        {"raw": "...", "name": "second", "fields": {"ceiling": "20"}, "error": ""}
   495	
   496	    A record with a non-empty ``error`` is reported back to the owner rather than
   497	    applied, so a typo is answered instead of ignored.  Nothing outside an
   498	    ``ACCOUNTS:`` line is looked at: the rest of the comment is prose.
   499	    """
   500	    out: list[dict] = []
   501	    for line in (text or "").splitlines():
   502	        match = DIRECTIVE_RE.match(line)
   503	        if not match:
   504	            continue
   505	        record = {"raw": sanitize(line.strip(), 200), "name": "", "fields": {},
   506	                  "error": ""}
   507	        tokens = match.group("rest").split()
   508	        name = tokens[0] if tokens else ""
   509	        if not NAME_RE.match(name or ""):
   510	            record["error"] = (f"the first word after 'ACCOUNTS:' must be an account "
   511	                               f"name matching {NAME_RE.pattern}, got {name!r}")
   512	            out.append(record)
   513	            continue
   514	        record["name"] = name
   515	        for token in tokens[1:]:
   516	            assignment = ASSIGN_RE.match(token)
   517	            if not assignment:
   518	                record["error"] = (f"{token!r} is not a 'field=value' assignment; the "
   519	                                   "form is 'ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> "
   520	                                   "[reserved=<n>] [enabled=true|false]'")
   521	                break
   522	            key = assignment.group("key").lower()
   523	            if key not in DIRECTIVE_FIELDS:
   524	                record["error"] = (f"field {key!r} may not be set from a comment; this "
   525	                                   f"channel carries {', '.join(DIRECTIVE_FIELDS)} only "
   526	                                   "(an endpoint or a codex home is a path on the host "
   527	                                   "and is set with accounts.sh)")
   528	                break
   529	            record["fields"][key] = assignment.group("value")
   530	        if not record["error"] and not record["fields"]:
   531	            record["error"] = ("no field to set; the form is 'ACCOUNTS: <name> "
   532	                               "ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>] [enabled=true|false]'")
   533	        out.append(record)
   534	    return out

   540	
   541	    Each line begins with ``applied:`` or ``rejected:`` and names the account and

   543	    rejected directive never blocks the others: the owner gets one answer per

item.text: The malformed-file fallback is a real contract failure: `ready_report.py` retries through strict `run_mode.load_mode()`, and the inbox writes its “applied” ledger before the live file has loaded or saved. I am now pruning overlap so each final finding identifies one repairable defect rather than counting the same failure twice.

Because the new schema explicitly makes those names ordinary and their homes editable, this can run work under the wrong credential and defeat per-key ceilings.

 # Protocol: full speed mode — the briefing, the mode file, the standing reports
 
 Normative for a *run*: a bounded period in which the fleet works at the owner's
 stated capacity and speed. Read `local/protocols/meta.md` first, then this file
 before starting or pausing a run.
 
 The rule this protocol exists to enforce: **the owner gives one briefing and
 afterwards receives only the estimate one-liner and the progress log.** Every
 number the owner states lives in exactly one file, and every component reads it
 through one tool. Nothing is transcribed by hand into a second place — on
 2026-09-12 the caps were restated five times, edited by hand ten times, and a
 resume script still announced "primary 5 / second 39 / total 44" forty minutes
 after those numbers were wrong.
 
 ## 1. The briefing
 
 The owner copies the committed template
 `results/telemetry/owner-tools/run-brief.template.json` to
 `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/run-brief.json` and edits the values. That is
 the **only** artifact the owner authors for a run.

    21	# truth for which keys exist, what their CEILINGS are, and whether the pipeline may

    23	# tick and every reservation, so a change here reaches admission within 60 seconds
    24	# with no session prompted, no brief re-applied and nothing restarted.

    27	# below it and may never exceed `ceiling - external_reserved`.  Lowering it takes
    28	# effect at the next tick; raising it lets the additive creep continue.
    29	# `enabled false` is cap 0 immediately and no probes, and so is `remove`.
    30	#
    31	# Raising a ceiling is a PERMISSION, not a jump: AIMD then creeps +1 per quiet
    32	# window (120 s by default) and only while the key is saturated, so ten recovered
    33	# slots take twenty minutes of real demand.  `accounts.sh cap <name> <n>` is the
    34	# one immediate lever — it sets the effective cap now, clamped to the ceiling and
    35	# recorded by the controller.  Set the ceiling first; the cap cannot exceed it.

     us instead of the owner typing ``PAR=8`` (2026-09-12 05:44Z).  The lower
